items.title: Agric ministry puts post-harvest loss at $10bn yearly
items.description: •As 14 of 17 federal silos fail •20% of grains, 70% of fruits, vegetables lost By Gabriel Ewepu ABUJA — THE Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, Senator Abubakar Kyari, Tuesday, disclosed that Nigeria loses an estimated $10 billion annually to post-harvest losses. Kyari made this known as one of the panelists focusing on the topic ‘Productivity Revolution for Growth’ at the ongoing 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit (NES#32) organised by the Nigerian Economic Summit Group, NESG, in Abuja. He also said Nigeria loses between 15 and 20 per cent of its grains, including rice, maize and millet, while losses involving tomatoes, pepper, onions, fruits and vegetables could reach 60 to 70 per cent, depending on the season. He described the reduction of post-harvest losses as a low-hanging fruit in Nigeria’s food security drive, said the country could significantly improve food availability and farmers’ earnings by addressing weaknesses in storage, processing, transportation and market infrastructure. He stated: “We lose almost about $10 billion annually on post-harvest losses. “About 15 to 20 per cent on grains, and you can see grains that are hard, and you probably think we will not lose much of that, but we lose on grains, on cereal, rice, maize, and so on and so forth, millet. On fruits and vegetables, the minister warned that the scale of waste was considerably higher. “Tomato, pepper, onion, and other fruits and vegetables, we lose some of that as high as 60 to 70 per cent depending on the season”, Kyari said, attributing the vulnerability of tomatoes, in particular, to their short shelf life and the effects of hot weather. The Minister also lamented that 17 of the 33 silo complexes built by the Federal Government had been concessioned to private operators, but only three were performing. “The government had concessioned 17 out of the 33 silos that it had built over a period of time, but I’ll tell you that out of the 17, only three have performed. All the 14 are almost comatose for the past, I believe, since when it was concessioned”, he said. The minister attributed the problem partly to a disconnect between agricultural production centres and the location of storage facilities. According to him, some farming communities are situated more than 100 kilometres from major storage facilities, making it difficult and costly for farmers to transport their produce to the silos. He argued that the country’s storage strategy must be redesigned to reflect the geographical distribution of agricultural production rather than depend exclusively on large-scale facilities located far from farming communities. The minister’s position suggests that the challenge extends beyond the physical availability of silos to questions of accessibility, operational efficiency, commercial viability and the suitability of infrastructure to the needs of farmers. To address the shortcomings, he (Kyari) said the Federal Government was considering smaller, modern community silo systems that could be deployed closer to farming communities. He explained that the proposed facilities would draw inspiration from traditional grain-storage practices, while incorporating modern technology, ventilation and renewable energy. The facilities, he said, could be designed to accommodate capacities of 2,000, 3,000, 5,000 or 10,000 tonnes, depending on the productive capacity of the communities they serve. He said: “We need not only the huge silo systems, but we need community silo systems.” He noted that traditional grain-storage structures, known in Hausa as grumbu, offered a useful starting point for developing storage systems adapted to local conditions. He said the government was exploring modernised versions of such systems, equipped with appropriate ventilation and solar-powered infrastructure. “We have renewable energy that we must take advantage of because we have to have that in our budget”, he said. The proposed approach could reduce the distance farmers travel to store produce, improve access to preservation facilities and help prevent avoidable losses caused by inadequate storage. However, the effectiveness of the initiative will depend on implementation, maintenance, affordability and the ability of farmers and cooperatives to access the facilities when they need them. Beyond post-harvest losses, the Minister said the government’s approach to food security had evolved from its traditional emphasis on the availability, accessibility and affordability of food to include consumption of nutritious and diverse diets. He asserted that food security must be assessed not only by the volume of food produced or available in markets, but also by whether households can consume nutritious food capable of supporting healthy growth, particularly among children. The minister also disclosed that agriculture had assumed a higher level of national coordination, with the Presidential Food Systems Coordinating Unit bringing together relevant sectors, including agriculture, water resources, environment and health, to address interconnected food security and nutrition challenges. The approach recognises that food security is influenced by several factors, including agricultural productivity, water availability, environmental conditions, public health and nutrition. He also noted the fragmented structure of Nigerian agriculture as a major obstacle to improving productivity. He said between 85 and 90 per cent of Nigerian farmers were smallholders, with the average farm size standing at approximately 0.6 hectares, equivalent to 6,000 square metres. items.title: Constitutional questions
items.description: PAKISTAN has had three constitutions. Two given to it by its people in 1956 and 1973. One promulgated by a field marshal in 1962. The 1973 Constitution was adopted by the people through their representatives in the constituent assembly. Article 1 states that Pakistan shall be a federal republic. Neither the term “federal” nor “republic” is expressly defined. The Objectives Resolution provides guidance. The power and authority of the state in our republic is to be exercised through the chosen representatives of the people. A republic is distinct from rule by one man. In a republic, rulers are not immune from accountability. They can be removed and replaced if they fail to perform. The various territories that are part of Pakistan or that accede to Pakistan form a federation. These territories are autonomous and their boundaries and powers and authority are prescribed. The Objectives Resolution guarantees that the integrity of the territories shall be safeguarded. A federal state is brought into being by the territories that comprise it through a written instrument. This instrument defines the authority of the federation and these territories. The federation presupposes and is premised on the existence of these territories. Dismantling the territories would undermine the foundational integrity of the federation and the compact reflected in the 1973 Constitution. A constitution can be amended. The limits of a province or territory can be changed with its consent. Such an amendment may alter limits or provincial boundaries. It does not contemplate partition or subdivision of existing provinces or existing territories. Actions that compromise provincial integrity inevitably lead to questions regarding the benefits of being part of the federation. These questions have been resolved by the various territories and reflected in the 1973 Constitution. It would not be wise to reopen them. Emergency powers cannot be used to deprive any citizen of the right to a fair trial. Provincial integrity is not incompatible with devolution of power and effective local government. The Principles of Policy of the Constitution require the state to encourage local government institutions. Each province is constitutionally required to establish a local government system and to devolve power. The president is the head of state and represents the unity of the republic. The president as a symbol of a united federation must be satisfied prior to provincial autonomy being assailed. This can only be done in exceptional circumstances. The emergency provisions enable federal rule over a province if the president is satisfied that certain conditions exist. The president does not have authority to impo­­se an emergency whenever he deems fit. The eme­rgency provisions are not like the erstwhile Arti­cle 58(2)(b). The president was empowered under this Article to dissolve an elected government in his discretion. The emergency powers are not exp­ressed to be discretionary powers of the president. Could the president have refused to sign the recent emergency proclamation notwithstanding the advice of the federal government? He could certainly have asked the government to look at matters again. Did he have discretion to refuse if after reconsideration the government insisted? The term “discretion” is not used in the relevant Articles of the Constitution. The conventional legal view is that absent a power being expressed as discretionary, the president is bound to act on the advice of the government. In the case of the emergency provisions the president is required to be “satisfied”. This suggests a mental state of an individual office holder. It could be argued that a mental state cannot be imposed through governmental advice. Regardless, in the present emergency, this appears to be a moot point since the president did not even ask the government to re­­c­onsider its advice. We do not know the nature of the material made available to the president to satisfy him beyond what is contained in the proclamation. Its contents are in substance assertions and non-speaking. They do not provide cogent reasons. If the stipulated conditions for an emergency do not exist, the proclamation is unlawful. It is incorrect to state that because emergency powers exist in the Constitution, the exercise thereof is constitutional. The existence of a power and its lawful exercise are two distinct matters. Emergency powers cannot be used to deprive any citizen of Pakistan of the right to a fair trial. The emergency provisions enable suspension of operation of a provision of the Constitution only relating to a body or authority in the province. They do not permit the suspension of Article 10-A of the Constitution which provides for a fair trial and due process. The federal government’s order pursuant to the proclamation states that Article 175(3) shall not apply to the designated districts. This Article provides for separation of the judiciary from the executive. The constitutional framework does not contemplate such suspension. The emergency provisions also do not authorise the subdivision of a province by creating a separate governance structure for certain designated parts absent provincial legislative consent. Where certain federally administered areas have been made part of a province through a constitutional amendment (as is the case with Fata), the impact of this amendment cannot lawfully be undone through a proclamation of emergency which is an executive action. Depriving people of a territory of rule by their representatives is undemocratic and diminishes the federation. When imposed on an unwilling provincial government, it pits the centre against one of its parts and weakens the whole. Normal constitutional functioning should be restored as soon as possible. The real question that needs consideration is whether currently Pakistan is truly operating as a federal republic. That is what is contemplated by the first Article of our Constitution. If the compact that binds the territories that comprise our nation is broken, what credible vision can the rulers offer the people in these territories? The existential challenge the country faces is not from its enemies and those who wish us ill. It is from power being divorced from political authority and therefore accountability. That is the real emergency facing us. Until we confront this truth, the story of Pakistan will not change. The writer is a lawyer. Published in Dawn, October 28th, 2026

items.title: Vote-buying: NDC weighs rules to distinguish transport payments from electoral inducement
items.description: The National Democratic Congress (NDC) is weighing rules to determine when money given to delegates for transport becomes an electoral inducement. Former Tamale Central MP Inusah Fuseini says proposed constitutional changes must address payments that exceed reasonable travel costs, even when candidates describe them as transport support. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Tuesday, he said the party needed clear standards for acceptable payments. “How much money can we say is appropriate in the circumstances? If somebody gives a delegate GH¢200, is it an inducement or what is it?” His comments follow reports of widespread alleged vote-buying during the NDC’s latest constituency executive elections. Mr Fuseini said declaring the purpose of a payment did not resolve the question. The amount could still exceed what a delegate reasonably needed for transportation. The committee reviewing the party’s constitution is examining how to handle such cases. It must also establish which party body can investigate complaints and impose sanctions. “So we need a framework.” Mr Fuseini said the committee had recognised the need for sanctions after acknowledging that inducement had occurred in the elections. But it found “there was no legal mechanism in our constitution to deal with that”. He explained that this gap could expose disciplinary decisions to challenges. The party needed rules that define misconduct and give its institutions authority to act. One option is to empower constituency councils of elders to handle cases locally. Another is referring offenders to the national headquarters, where the Functional Executive Committee would act. The party would further review the proposals before presenting them to a special congress for constitutional amendment. “So yes, it’s a work in progress.” Mr Fuseini also warned that the growing financial demands of politics were excluding women, young people and people with integrity. Some potential candidates lacked the resources to compete. Others were withdrawing from politics because of the sums involved. He said heavy spending also pressured politicians to recoup their money after winning office. “A politician is not an NGO, and so when people spend that amount of money, they expect to recoup that, and that fuels corruption on a national scale.”

items.title: Miners’ deaths: Panel recommends summary dismissal, prosecution of NSCDC officers, N1.4bn for victims
items.description: •Says overcrowding, heat stress, dehydration caused deaths •Rules out use of chemicals; as FG vows justice By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA—An independent ministerial committee has recommended summary dismissal, administrative sanctions and prosecution of some officers of the Nigerian Security and Civil Defence Corps, NSCDC, over the deaths of 33 detainees in the custody of its Niger State command in Minna, along with N1.4 billion in compensation for victims and survivors. The committee’s chairman, Jonathan Kure, who presented the report to the Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, in Abuja, yesterday, described the deaths as “entirely preventable.” Kure said the committee concluded that the incident was a preventable custodial tragedy, caused by severe overcrowding, unlawful and unsuitable detention conditions, failure of duty of care, disregard of repeated distress warnings, inadequate supervision, and wider systemic deficiencies. He said the evidence did not support claims that the deaths resulted from a disease outbreak. According to him, “available medical and forensic evidence instead indicated that the fatalities resulted from an environmental asphyxia, an acute respiratory failure caused by prolonged confinement in a severely overcrowded and poorly ventilated detention cell, aggravated by heat stress and dehydration.” The 65-page report, of which 46 pages form the main body, examined the arrest, detention, treatment and deaths of detainees between September 15 and 17, 2026. It was commissioned by the minister, following a presidential directive. The committee said the tragedy stemmed from enforcement operations against suspected illegal mining in and around Minna. No headquarter’s approval Kure said: “The operation was undertaken without an approved operational order, proper planning and consultation with relevant mining authorities, or involvement of the specialised Mining Marshals unit. National headquarters was not informed before the operation commenced,” he added. He said the raids led to the arrest of men, women and children, and that by the evening of September 16, 75 persons had been detained. He said after one release, 74 remained in custody overnight, with about 50 male detainees confined in a cell measuring about 20 square metres. The committee said the cell had “a solid metal door, inadequate airflow, no running water, poor lighting, and no functioning toilet.” It said food and drinking water were either unavailable or grossly inadequate, adding that adults and minors were held together. It found that the conditions breached constitutional safeguards, the Administration of Criminal Justice Act, the Child Rights Act and accepted international standards. The committee concluded that they “amounted to cruel, inhuman, and degrading treatment, and created an environment, in which fatalities became foreseeable and preventable.” Kure said signs of distress began shortly after 7pm on September 16 and continued through the night. “Detainees repeatedly banged on cell doors and walls, shouted for assistance, and pleaded for water,” he said. “These distress calls were heard by officers assigned to nearby duties,” he said. He said medical personnel had earlier raised concerns about poor ventilation and the risk of suffocation, but “were not acted upon.” Officers, he said, “failed to open the cell, decongest the facility, or arrange emergency intervention.” The deaths occurred inside the male cell between 8pm on September 16 and 7am on September 17, 2026. “By the time the cell was opened, many detainees had died,” Kure said. The committee authenticated 33 deaths, 14 of them minors, and identified 41 survivors, adding that the higher figures reported immediately after the incident “could not be reconciled with available records and identified victims.” Though some survivors alleged that an aerosol substance was sprayed into the cell before the deaths, Kure said the committee found no evidence to support this claim and concluded that the allegation remained unproven on the available evidence. The committee held individual officers responsible, stressing that the State Commandant, Suberu Siaka, authorised and supervised the operation without proper planning, approval or oversight, giving rise to overcrowding. It said the Head of the Investigation Unit, T. S. Sodiq, facilitated unlawful detention practices, ignored legal and medical concerns, and failed to act, despite direct awareness of the deteriorating conditions. SC Usman Ndamaka was accused of maintaining overcrowded conditions, instructing subordinates not to open the cell, failing to respond to emergency alerts, and taking part in the cleaning and alteration of the detention area before independent examination. The committee said ASC I Hassan Mohammed failed to open the cell, despite repeated distress signals and did not adequately escalate the emergency, while DSC Abubakar Dabang profiled the suspects into detention, including minors, and failed to protect their rights and properly document exhibits. It said DSC Musa Marafat unlawfully arrested and detained Emmanuel Emeka over a civil debt dispute unrelated to mining, contributing directly to his continued unlawful detention until his death. Beyond individual misconduct, it identified institutional weaknesses in the NSCDC, including “inadequate detention infrastructure, lack of effective custodial oversight, absence of CCTV monitoring systems, weak documentation practices, poor emergency medical capability, ineffective supervision, weak intelligence reporting arrangements, workforce imbalance, and chronic underfunding.” It said these deficiencies created an environment in which serious violations occurred and “would continue to occur without timely detention intervention.” Committee listed limitations. The detention register for 16th September 2026 was unavailable, 30 of the 33 deceased were buried before post-mortem examinations, and the detention area was cleaned, disinfected and altered before independent forensic investigators arrived. It nonetheless concluded that “sufficient evidence existed to establish the essential facts, causes, and responsibilities.” On accountability, the committee recommended “summary dismissal of officers found primarily responsible; prosecution for offences, including murder, criminal negligence, torture, and inhuman treatment where applicable; as well as investigation by anti-corruption agencies into allegations of extortion and exhibit mismanagement.” It also recommended administrative sanctions for officers whose failures contributed to the incident but “did not amount to primary culpability.” On compensation, the committee recommended N30 million for each of the 33 bereaved families and N10 million for each of the 41 survivors, totalling N1.4 billion. It also recommended educational support for dependents of the deceased, medical rehabilitation for survivors, psychological support for affected families, and a formal apology by the federal government. To prevent a recurrence, it recommended construction of standard detention facilities across all NSCDC commands, installation of closed-circuit television, CCTV, systems in custodial areas, an independent inspectorate and custodial oversight mechanism, enhanced custodial management and human rights training, among others. Kure appealed for political will to ensure the recommendations were brought to implementation.” FG vows justice Receiving the report, the Minister, Tunji-Ojo, said: “I want to assure you, nothing will be swept under the carpet.” He recalled that after the committee’s inauguration, he went to see President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, “and I never saw him more passionate about justice than that day. The era of setting up committees just to downplay tension is not now.’’ He said the 10-member committee was carefully chosen, adding that none of the members was appointee of government. He said there would be “a complete review” of the NSCDC, as the government had done in the Nigeria Immigration Service, and Correctional Service and the Fire Service. He said: “A single bad apple shouldn’t describe the apple tree. But, of course, of those that have goofed, there will be repercussions.” The minister said officers who concealed or doctored evidence must be suspended with immediate effect, pending internal investigation and other disciplinary action. “You cannot destroy evidence in a case where we lost 30-something people. That is wickedness,” he said. Tunji-Ojo said the report would be forwarded to the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice for judicial action where necessary. He added that the ministry would work with the NSCDC to ensure “that a body, an agency set up to protect Nigerians does not end up hurting Nigerians. “To the families of the deceased, we want to assure you, this government will never leave you alone. We will make sure justice is done to serve the memory of the lost ones.” The post Miners’ deaths: Panel recommends summary dismissal, prosecution of NSCDC officers, N1.4bn for victims appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Senanu questions NDC’s commitment to tackling vote-buying
items.description: Anti-corruption campaigner Edem Senanu has criticised the National Democratic Congress (NDC) leadership for what he considers an inadequate response to allegations of vote-buying during the party’s recent constituency executive elections, warning that the handling of the matter risks damaging the party’s image and ethical standing. He said the party should demonstrate accountability by committing to investigate credible allegations, rather than appearing to suggest that action would depend on evidence supplied by its own members. Mr Senanu made the comments on Joy News’ PM Express on Tuesday, October 27, in reaction to remarks by the NDC National Deputy General Secretary, Rashid Tanko, on the controversy surrounding the internal elections. “I find [Rashid] Tanko’s response challenging and not demonstrating adequate leadership in terms of accountability,” he said. Mr Senanu argued that responsible party leadership should welcome evidence of possible wrongdoing from any source and take steps to establish the facts, irrespective of whether the information came from within or outside the party. He said the suggestion that the party needed evidence from its own people before being satisfied that vote-buying had occurred was troubling and could undermine efforts to address the practice. “That kind of implication, that trajectory does not carry us all along. We won’t get you the results you want,” he said. Timing of gifts raises questions Mr Senanu said the timing of the distribution of items, including television sets, during the constituency elections raised questions about the intentions behind the gifts. He explained that vote-buying involved the provision of an inducement by a political party, candidate or representative with the intention of securing the recipient’s vote. “In this context, you cannot tell me that these TVs and what have you were flying a month ago. They were happening at the exact time. So the intention of what they wanted to achieve is there,” he said. He maintained that whether candidates who distributed the items eventually won or lost was not the central issue. “Whether they won or not is not material,” he said. According to him, the timing of the alleged distribution was an important consideration in determining whether the items were intended to influence delegates’ choices. “The extent that these things were being given at that time tells us there was a clear intention to harvest votes,” he said. The claims, however, require proper investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the distribution of the items and whether they were intended to influence voting decisions. Calls for prompt investigation Mr Senanu said the absence of a sufficiently firm response from the party leadership, nearly 48 hours after the issue was raised, was worrying and risked conveying the impression that the allegations were not being treated with the seriousness they deserved. He said the party’s reputation could suffer even if the evidence did not come from its own members. “If it’s not your own people who are providing the evidence, but it’s available, it taints the image. It reduces the ethical standards of the party,” he said. He called on the leadership to adopt a more proactive approach by inviting anyone with relevant information to submit it and then initiating an investigation. “I would rather leadership say that we haven’t seen it, but please provide it. We will immediately ensure that we look into the matter,” he said. Mr Senanu said such a response would demonstrate a commitment to accountability and reassure members and the public that the party was prepared to confront allegations of wrongdoing within its ranks. “That’s the way that we demonstrate responsiveness and accountable leadership,” he added. He expressed concern that the passage of time without a clear response suggested the party might not fully appreciate the seriousness of the matter. “Forty-eight hours after, and we still haven’t seen, we haven’t heard. That is very worrying. It does not show a sensitivity to the fact that this is a very important issue, and it suggests that the party itself is not taking this as serious enough,” he said. Electoral integrity at stake The controversy has renewed attention on the role of money and gifts in internal party elections, where candidates compete for positions that influence party organisation and leadership. Mr Senanu’s argument is that the integrity of such contests must be protected regardless of whether the alleged inducements change the final outcome. A credible response, he said, requires party officials to examine the available evidence, explain their actions and demonstrate that rules on electoral conduct are taken seriously. The NDC’s handling of the allegations is therefore likely to be judged not only by the findings of any investigation but also by how promptly and transparently the party responds to concerns about its internal democratic processes.

items.title: Netanyahu and rival each claim mandate after tight Israel election
items.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and rival Gadi Eisenkot each vowed on Wednesday to form a government after both came up short in the first election since the events of October 7, 2023. Voters turned out Tuesday in the highest numbers in decades to give their verdict on the divisive rule of Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister who has pushed the country sharply to the right and unleashed a wave of wars in response to the Hamas attack. Exit polls showed Eisenkot, a former military chief and political novice, and his opposition bloc neck and neck with Netanyahu’s hard-right camp and both well away from the threshold for a majority in parliament. The strongest gains came from Arab Israeli parties whose voters turned out in soaring numbers against Netanyahu, who has relentlessly warned that the minority would dilute the Jewish nationalist direction in which he has taken Israel. Netanyahu, greeting cheering supporters at a Jerusalem convention centre after 0100 GMT, called for a “strong government of the right” and said that the “Jewish and Zionist majority must unite”. The 77-year-old prime minister was unusually brief and did not directly claim victory. Instead, he listed leaders Israel has killed under his orders and again hinted that he was ready for a third bombing campaign against Iran alongside US President Donald Trump, his close ally. “Israel has a unique opportunity with our partner President Trump to forever eliminate the existential threat of Iran,” Netanyahu said. Eisenkot, speaking to his own supporters in Tel Aviv, issued a veiled warning to Netanyahu, who observers say could use a war to push for a unity government. “Netanyahu, don’t you dare use Israel’s security for your political needs,” Eisenkot said. Addressing Israel’s security establishment, Eisenkot said that they served the state and not Netanyahu, calling him “a caretaker prime minister, without a mandate or the people’s trust”. ‘Public has voted for change’ Eisenkot shares many of Netanyahu’s views on security and has backed the Gaza offensive following October 7 that has reduced the territory to rubble . But Eisenkot has vowed to create a more inclusive atmosphere inside Israel and to rein in extremist settlers in the West Bank who have attacked Palestinians with virtual impunity. After turnout of nearly 78 per cent, the highest since 1999, Eisenkot said it would be a mistake to hold a second election and vowed to work “swiftly” to form a government. Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot (R) arrives to address his supporters at the election night rally after the first exit polls were announced, in Tel Aviv on early October 28, 2026, during Israel’s legislative elections. — AFP “The public has voted for change,” Eisenkot said. “A worthy leader would accept the people’s vote of no confidence and announce his retirement from political life today.” The three mainstream Israeli television networks in exit polls gave the two blocs each around 51 seats – well below the 61 needed to govern – after initially giving an edge to the opposition. Israeli Arab lists were projected to win 17 to 18 seats, a sharp gain, with some Israeli Arab communities reporting near-universal turnout driven by outrage to often derogatory rhetoric against them by Netanyahu’s far-right allies. Key Israeli Arab leader Mansour Abbas said he believed the right had “suffered a major loss” and was open to working with Eisenkot. But Eisenkot said during the campaign he would not govern with Israeli Arab lawmakers — and Netanyahu again suggested that a government relying on Arab votes would lack legitimacy. Arab lawmakers could give Eisenkot support in parliamentary votes to maintain a minority government without joining a coalition. If not, Israel could head to new elections. Itamar Ben Gvir , a far-right firebrand who according to exit polls did not gain as much as many expected, warned Netanyahu against another option — a unity government with Eisenkot. “It would be a terrible mistake,” said Ben Gvir, who champions the expulsion of Palestinians and would likely be excluded from any unity government. Hebrew University of Jerusalem political scientist Gideon Rahat said Ben Gvir had succeeded in mobilising votes — of Israeli Arabs. But he said: “Even if Netanyahu lost, that doesn’t mean Eisenkot won.” Divisive The election came as Israel looks increasingly isolated on the world stage, driven by the war in Iran and the military campaign in Gaza, soaring settlement construction and violence in the occupied West Bank. Netanyahu himself faces an arrest warrant from the International Criminal Court over Gaza as well as domestic corruption charges that could land him in prison if he loses power. Eisenkot is a political novice whose mild manner is the antithesis of the smooth-talking incumbent. The son of working-class Moroccan Jewish immigrants, Eisenkot would be the first prime minister of Middle Eastern or North African descent. Before voting, the 66-year-old Eisenkot paid his respects privately at the grave of his son Gal, whose death fighting in Gaza has drawn empathy from many Israelis. Tens of thousands of Israelis are estimated to have flown in from abroad for an election seen as crucial for their country. Eilana Zisblit, 55, told AFP she had travelled back from Canada, where she has lived for almost 30 years, to vote for a centre-right party in Eisenkot’s bloc. “The country is going in a really, really bad direction. Both for Jews and Arabs living in the country, and for Jews living abroad,” she said. The time to act is “now, or the country really won’t survive anymore”.

items.title: Atiku to Tinubu: $20.5bn loan plan vindicates my warning
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike Former Vice President and African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, has said President Bola Tinubu’s request for approval to borrow $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion vindicates his earlier warning about a proposed $20 billion loan, accusing the administration of failing to disclose the specific projects the funds would finance. Atiku said the absence of project-by-project details raises questions about transparency and the possibility of public funds being channelled to political allies and favoured contractors, particularly through the Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway project, which he alleged had been rerouted inland. In a statement by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku recalled that he had warned on October 12 about the reported borrowing plan and challenged Tinubu to confirm or deny it and publish the relevant accounts. “Today, he has asked the Senate to approve $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion in external loans. My warning has been vindicated,” he said. Atiku faulted the President for failing to provide details of the projects, their costs, locations and contractors, insisting that Nigerians should not be asked to shoulder such a huge debt without knowing how the money would be spent. He questioned whether the highway project could become a conduit for directing borrowed funds to political allies, especially with an election approaching. “Is this a development plan for Nigerians or a campaign financing scheme dressed up as infrastructure?” he asked. The ADC candidate warned that he would scrutinise loans obtained during the final year of Tinubu’s administration if elected President, vowing to challenge any borrowing found to have breached constitutional, statutory or due process requirements. “I put local and international lenders on notice: any loan granted to this winding-down administration must meet all constitutional, statutory and due process requirements,” he said. He urged the National Assembly to withhold approval until the President publishes the projects, contracts, costs, contractors, loan terms and repayment obligations attached to the borrowing plan. “No public money should be borrowed in the dark, and no lawmaker should sign a blank cheque against Nigeria’s future,” Atiku said. He said the burden of proof rested on Tinubu to demonstrate that the loans would serve the national interest rather than political interests, warning that Nigerians struggling with the cost of living should not be made to pay for debts incurred without adequate public disclosure. Atiku said the controversy could further shape the political contest, with voters having an opportunity to hold the administration accountable for its borrowing decisions. The post Atiku to Tinubu: $20.5bn loan plan vindicates my warning appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Sommet Russie-Afrique: Moscou en opération séduction pour cette troisième édition
items.description: Le coup d'envoi du troisième sommet Russie-Afrique est donné ce mercredi 28 octobre à Moscou. Le format est identique aux deux premières éditions, organisées à Sotchi en 2019 et à Saint-Pétersbourg en 2023 : deux jours de discussions et de réunions, cette fois en plein cœur de la capitale, dans un cadre prestigieux, avec un Vladimir Poutine particulièrement impliqué. À défaut de résultats probants jusque-là, la Russie veut donner l'impression de soigner ses invités et faire la démonstration de son influence sur le continent.

items.title: FG, NLC reach deal on N70,000 transport allowance, 19-month health workers’ arrears
items.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young The Federal Government and the Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, have reached an agreement on a series of measures to ease the economic difficulties facing workers, including a ₦70,000 transport intervention and the payment of 19 months’ arrears owed health workers. The resolutions were reached at a conciliation meeting held at the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment yesterday, following an earlier meeting convened on October 22. The meetings were organised to address concerns raised by the NLC over the rising cost of living, the implementation of the National Minimum Wage, petroleum pump prices, workers’ welfare and outstanding allowances. The agreement was signed on behalf of the federal government by Dr. Muhammad Maigari Dingyadi, Minister of Labour and Employment; Timi Yakubu, Director-General, Budget; and Dr. Garba Abdul S. U., Permanent Secretary (SWO), Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, while NLC president, Joe Ajaero, and National Secretary, JNPSNC, Olowoyo Gbenga, stood for labour. Under the agreement, the federal government will provide a transport intervention of N70,000 across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026. The government also approved peculiar allowance with effect from May 1, 2026, while payment of the arrears is expected to begin in November and will be made in three equal monthly instalments. In addition, the 19 months’ outstanding allowances owed health workers is to be paid within three months, beginning in December 2026. The meeting also agreed that the Minimum Wage Negotiation Committee would be constituted to commence work immediately. However, the parties remained divided over the effective date for implementing the new minimum wage. On the issue of tax relief for workers, the meeting resolved that the matter would be referred to the National Executive Council, as taxation is a statutory issue. Meanwhile, the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security has submitted the list of beneficiaries and the cost implications of the proposed hazard allowance for agricultural officers to the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission for verification. The verification is expected to be completed within two weeks, after which the commission will issue an implementation template. Similarly, the NSIWC is expected to complete an updated assessment of the cost implications of the proposed CONHESS adjustment within three weeks. The assessment will enable the Presidential Committee on Salaries to take a decision on the matter. The federal government and NLC urged state and local governments to participate in the intervention process and implement the agreed measures. The parties also agreed to reconvene after one month to review the level of implementation of the resolutions. The post FG, NLC reach deal on N70,000 transport allowance, 19-month health workers’ arrears appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Abascal teme que Feijóo descuide al votante de centro por disputarle su electorado
items.description: A Santiago Abascal le preocupa que el presidente del PP, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, este asumiendo cada vez más su discurso, hasta el punto de que, en algunas materias, parecen prácticamente indiferenciables para los electores, según fuentes de Vox. Puede resultar paradójico, ya que este hecho evidencia que Abascal ha ganado la batalla ideológica en el seno de la derecha, tras quejarse durante años de que los populares habían asumido sin discutirlos los postulados de la izquierda. Además, esta evolución de Feijóo facilita que los dos socios puedan pactar un programa de gobierno común después de las elecciones del 29 de noviembre. Seguir leyendo

items.title: José María Ridao: “El temor de una incidencia de la ley de nietos en el resultado electoral es difícil de sostener con las cifras”
items.description: El escritor y diplomático José María Ridao (Madrid, 1961) lleva décadas tratando de interpretar lo que pasa en el mundo; sobre el terreno, desde su trabajo en embajadas y consulados, y sobre el papel, con ensayos, novelas y artículos periodísticos . Ha vivido en legaciones en la extinta Unión Soviética, Estados Unidos o la India. Ahora se encuentra al frente del Consulado de Buenos Aires, el mayor de España en el mundo, y uno de los más afectados por la ley de nietos. Accede a una entrevista telefónica a punto de que se cumpla un cuarto de siglo de su libro La elección de la barbarie (Tusquets, 2002), en el que tocaba muchos de los problemas que atraviesan hoy las democracias. Seguir leyendo

Pero, más allá de los cambios en las papeletas de las formaciones políticas, ¿cómo se reparten los escaños en ambas Cámaras? ¿Cuántos diputados y senadores corresponden por circunscripción? La explicación, en el vídeo superior. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Andrea Ropero (’El intermedio’): “Me alegra la expulsión de Vito Quiles del Congreso, a mí no me acreditan”
items.description: Dónde nacemos condiciona nuestra mirada. Andrea Ropero (Binaced, Huesca, 43 años) lo hizo en una familia de agricultores que tuvo que exiliarse por la Guerra Civil. Estudió en Barcelona con las becas de la educación pública. Y no se rindió gracias a su abuela. “Pasé una época muy mala y estuve a punto de dejar la carrera. ‘Mi mayor pena sería morirme y no verte de periodista’, me dijo. Al final, me vio en La Sexta. Antes del informativo, llamaba casa por casa en el pueblo para avisar a los vecinos”. Al recordarlo, los ojos verdes le brillan un poco más. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Mis niveles de testosterona están bajos, ¿y qué? Por qué se reivindica al hombre ‘blandito’
items.description: Hace apenas unos días, la revista norteamericana Inside Hook publicó un contenido periodístico del todo infrecuente. Lo firma el escritor neoyorquino Jaed Coffin y viene a ser un elogio del hombre “normal” como alternativa al superhombre nietzscheano de las redes sociales, además de una exhortación a dejarse de tanto gimnasio, “madurar bien” y aceptar con elegancia la derrota que nos impone el paso del tiempo. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Si Rajoy levantara la cabeza
items.description: El ser humano —y no digamos ya el gallego, que posee la patente de la morriña— tiende a la nostalgia, la “tristeza melancólica originada por el recuerdo de una dicha perdida”, según la RAE. La melancolía es vaga por naturaleza, paralizante, y cualquier tiempo pasado no siempre fue mejor, por mucho que siempre será más agradable recibir una carta de amor escrita a mano que un sexting intempestivo en el WhatsApp. Quizá es mucho decir que las campañas electorales de antes nos causaran “dicha”, pero en las de ahora, claramente, ha habido pérdidas: sobriedad, buen gusto, sentido del ridículo... Desde que los comicios generales tienen fecha, cuesta diferenciar las jornadas de precampaña en redes de cualquier episodio de La hora chanante , y cada vez es más difícil distinguir la realidad de las desternillantes sátiras de El Mundo Today. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Nacionalidad y sufragio: ¿Un binomio indestructible?
items.description: A la decisión del Tribunal Supremo, confirmando la suspensión cautelar del reconocimiento de nacionalidad realizado al amparo de la denominada Ley de nietos , se ha sumado el rechazo “por prematuro” del recurso de amparo ante el Tribunal Constitucional presentado por el Defensor del Pueblo. De este modo, todo apunta a que si el Supremo no adopta una resolución sobre el fondo de la controversia pendiente, avalando su corrección jurídica en tiempo útil, antes de que se celebren las elecciones generales el próximo 29 de noviembre (lo que resulta altamente improbable), las personas afectadas (unas 163.000) no podrán ejercer el derecho fundamental de sufragio. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Familias preocupadas por los llamamientos a protestar en Barcelona: “No sé si pondría la mano en el fuego por mi hijo”
items.description: ¿Qué estará haciendo mi hijo? ¿Habrá ido a la mani ? ¿Se habrá metido en algún lío? Son algunas de las preguntas que seguramente habrá inquietado a más de un padre o madre estos días al ver las imágenes de los graves altercados en Barcelona . Unas acciones que se convocan por redes sociales o por grupos de mensajería con cientos de personas y que las familias no acostumbran a controlar. “Las familias estamos muy preocupadas porque ves las imágenes de los disturbios y van a lo que van, a reventar cosas”, comenta Núria, madre de un adolescente a punto de cumplir 15 años. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La eterna asignatura pendiente de reformar la ‘ley mordaza’
items.description: La reforma de la ley de seguridad ciudadana, la conocida por sus detractores como ley mordaza , se ha convertido en la eterna asignatura pendiente de todos los gobiernos de Pedro Sánchez. Siempre prometida, pero nunca alcanzada. Durante la legislatura a la que acaba de poner fin el adelanto electoral, el proyecto ha navegado en una marejada de discrepancias entre los partidos que apoyan cambiar la norma hasta desembocar en una zozobra que se vislumbraba desde hace meses. A pesar de que, en octubre de 2024, el proyecto pasó su primer trámite parlamentario, en los dos años transcurridos desde entonces no ha llegado a reunirse la ponencia ―grupo de parlamentarios que estudian los proyectos legislativos antes de su envío a comisión y, si es aprobado, a pleno― precisamente por las diferencias entre los partidos que debían sumar sus votos para sacar adelante la iniciativa: PSOE, Sumar, EH Bildu, PNV, ERC, Podemos y Junts. Es la tercera vez que se frustra la reforma. En 2019, la causa fue la disolución anticipada de las Cortes. Y en 2023, el acuerdo sobre el texto entre socialistas, Unidas Podemos y los nacionalistas vascos fue rechazado por ERC, Junts, EH Bildu y BNG al considerarlo insuficiente. Seguir leyendo

items.description: Temor a la tribu, maltrato homosexual, obligaciones militares, miedo a la familia, disputas por una herencia e incluso amenazas en TikTok. items.title: El pacto migratorio de la UE deja a miles de solicitantes de asilo atrapados en las islas griegas
items.description: Shari Ful, bangladesí de 46 años, da un paseo junto a Kobir, Mohammad y Sagor por el puerto de Panagiuda. Al otro lado de la pequeña bahía se ve Kara Tepe, el campo de refugiados de Lesbos. Shari y sus amigos viven allí desde agosto. A su llegada presentaron una solicitud de asilo que fue inmediatamente rechazada. Han interpuesto un recurso, pero dan por hecho que este correrá la misma suerte porque Bangladés es uno de los países con la tasa más baja de resoluciones favorables en Grecia, donde no superó el 1% en el primer semestre de 2026, según Eurostat . Es jueves a media mañana, aunque todos los días se parecen cuando vives en un campo de refugiados. En la carretera de Kara Tepe a Mitilene, capital de la isla griega Lesbos, hay decenas de otros pequeños grupos de bangladesíes que deambulan para matar el tiempo mientras esperan la notificación de las resoluciones de sus recursos. items.title: Ramón Espinar, exdirigente de Podemos: “La vivienda no es una agenda de la izquierda, es un problema de país”
items.description: Ramón Espinar (Madrid, 40 años) se sienta en las escaleras del Planetario de Madrid, posa para las fotos y comienza a hacer bromas con una locuacidad casi supersónica. Dice que empezó en política muy joven y que joven era cuando salió ella, aunque en la conversación todo girará en torno a ella. A veces da la sensación de que es de los que lleva la procesión por dentro y saca el humor como legítima arma de defensa. Habrá hueco para hablar de orfandad y enfermedad, pero enseguida se abrazará a la risa. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Marcus Massalami, el primer ‘drag king’ de la franquicia ‘Drag Race’: “Ojalá tener en mi vida normal el 10% de la autoestima que tiene un hombre mediocre”
items.description: El concepto de travestismo suele ir ligado a lo femenino. Las drag queens más famosas han ofrecido una visión de la feminidad, muchas veces exagerada, a través del vestuario, el maquillaje y la gestualidad. Y esa ha sido la premisa del programa que la drag queen estadounidense RuPaul (California, 65 años) lanzó en 2009 bajo su propio nombre: RuPaul’s Drag Race , y que desde 2020 cuenta con su versión española. Un concurso de telerrealidad en el que varios artistas drag se enfrentan a pruebas para alzarse con el título de superestrella drag . Pero esa concepción cerrada se ha ido quedando pequeña con el paso de los años. A medida que el programa ganaba popularidad y se estrenaban ediciones en 14 países, ha ido dando espacio a nuevas realidades de eso que se llama travestismo. La sexta temporada de la edición española, emitida por Atresmedia, ha abierto nuevos horizontes con la inclusión de Marcus Massalami , el primer concursante exclusivamente drag king de toda la franquicia. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La coleta necesita una vuelta de goma más: por qué cada vez más mujeres se preocupan por la caída de pelo
items.description: No hay más cabellos de lo habitual en el desagüe de la ducha y tampoco se aprecian nuevas entradas al apartarse el flequillo o recogerse la melena al llegar a casa. Sin embargo, al hacerse una coleta, la goma necesita una vuelta más. La escena resulta familiar: cada vez más mujeres sienten que tienen menos pelo. Concretamente, según un estudio sobre salud capilar hecho público esta semana por Iraltone, un 46% de mujeres refiere más caída en el último año y un 28% de ellas, menos densidad (frente a un 36% y 24% respectivamente de hombres). El censo publicado en 2025 por la Sociedad internacional de cirugía capilar registró un aumento del 16,5% en el número de pacientes femeninas sometidas a cirugía capilar entre 2021 y 2024. El dato no demuestra que haya más alopecia, solo que más mujeres llegan a tratarla. En España, la Academia Española de Dermatología y Venereología (AEDV) calcula que la alopecia androgenética afecta a entre el 5% y el 10% de las mujeres y subraya una diferencia esencial: que se caiga más pelo no siempre significa que se esté perdiendo densidad. Entonces, ¿tenemos menos pelo o estamos prestándole más atención? Seguir leyendo

items.title: El alcohol no solo es una fuente de calorías vacías: también nos empuja a desear comida basura
items.description: Se estima que cada gramo de alcohol consumido aporta alrededor de siete kilocalorías ―una cifra muy cercana a la de las grasas― sin ofrecer a cambio al organismo ningún nutriente esencial como vitaminas, minerales, proteínas o fibra. De ahí el concepto de calorías vacías asociado a las bebidas alcohólicas . A esas calorías, además, habría que añadir, en el caso de los cócteles y combinados, las que aportan los refrescos azucarados. Por eso, el consumo de alcohol siempre se ha asociado con la ganancia de peso. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Un profesor agredido en las manifestaciones por la educación: “Era una fuerza bruta contra una gente totalmente pacífica”
items.description: Levantarse ha sido difícil en estos últimos días para Damián Bernabéu (Jaén, 63 años). Este profesor de Formación Profesional (FP), que llevaba 36 años ejerciendo hasta que se quedó en paro este verano, decidió unirse el 19 de octubre a las protestas de los docentes madrileños que están en huelga indefinida por la educación pública. La policía cargó contra Bernabéu y otros participantes frente al Palacio de Santoña, en el centro de la ciudad, a las puertas de un acto de la presidenta regional, Isabel Díaz Ayuso, mientras los profesores pedían mejorar las condiciones de un trabajo que él espera recuperar algún día. Un agente le empujó con un escudo policial, se cayó al suelo y se dio contra una pared. El impacto le dejó un gran moratón e hinchazón en la espalda que le provoca dolor cada vez que intenta levantarse de una silla o de la cama. Ahora ha presentado una denuncia en un juzgado de guardia por lo que considera una “fuerza bruta contra una gente totalmente pacífica”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Christopher Lloyd, el mítico Doc de ‘Regreso al futuro’, se sincera sobre sus adicciones en sus memorias: “Un par de rayas es todo lo que hizo falta”
items.description: En una sola semana, Christopher Lloyd, el científico loco de la trilogía ochentera Regreso al futuro , ha celebrado sus 88 años y ha publicado sus memorias, In My Own Time: A Memoir . Son más de 250 páginas en las que el actor recorre su solitaria infancia en Waveny (Connecticut); los inicios de su carrera actoral en el Nueva York de los años sesenta y su lucha contra la adicción al alcohol y a la cocaína, aspectos de su vida de los que rara vez ha hablado en público. En su libro cuenta que la primera ocasión que consumió drogas fue a las afueras de un club de comedia en Los Ángeles en los setenta. Se acercó al coche de una mujer a la que acababa de conocer y se metió “un par de rayas”. Según escribe: “Eso fue todo lo que hizo falta. Me enganché casi de inmediato. Me encantó, y ahí fue donde comenzó mi abuso de la cocaína”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Tinubu seeks $20.5bn, €1.04bn foreign loans to fund projects
items.description: *Seeks Reps’ approval for ₦269.4bn promissory notes to settle FG’s debts *Senate refers 2026–2027 supplementary borrowing plan to debt committee By Henry Umoru, Luminous Jannamike & Gift Odekina ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu has written the Senate, seeking an approval of a supplementary external borrowing plan of $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion to finance infrastructure and development projects across the country. He also asked the National Assembly to approve establishment and expansion of the Federal Government’s Promissory Note Programme to settle outstanding verified liabilities totalling N269.44 billion. President Tinubu’s letter was addressed to President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio. Akpabio, who read the letter yesterday at plenary, said the request covered the 2026–2027 fiscal period, targeting critical sectors, including power, transportation, agriculture, healthcare, education, water supply and security. Tinubu, who noted that the proposed borrowing is necessary to bridge Nigeria’s infrastructure funding gap, sustain economic growth, generate employment and improve the living conditions of Nigerians, urged the National Assembly to give the plan urgent consideration and approval to facilitate the timely release of funds and implementation of the projects. In the letter, the president said the proposed external financing will support projects and programmes spanning virtually every sector of the economy. “The 2026–2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan cuts across all sectors, with specific emphasis on infrastructure, agriculture, health, education, water supply, growth, security and employment generation, as well as financial management reforms, amongst others,” he said. According to the letter, the proposed facilities cost $20,517,755,901 and €1,045,083,643. It explained that the projects had been selected after technical and economic assessments. “I want to emphasise that the projects and programmes included in the borrowing plan were selected based on thorough technical and economic evaluation, as well as their anticipated contribution to the socio-economic development of the country,” he said. The president, who explained that the proposed investments were expected to create employment opportunities, promote skills acquisition, encourage entrepreneurship, reduce poverty and strengthen food security, said: “These initiatives aim to generate employment, promote skills acquisition, foster entrepreneurship, reduce poverty and enhance food security, all of which improve the livelihood of the Nigerian child.” ‘Loan is for projects in 36 states and FCT’ He disclosed that most of the projects would be executed across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, stressing that the nationwide spread of the interventions would help address development needs across the federation. Tinubu added that the scale of Nigeria’s infrastructure deficit and the financial resources required to address it had made additional external borrowing necessary. “In light of the need for significant infrastructure investment in the country and the vast financial resources needed to address this gap, it has become essential to pursue broader external borrowings to close the financing shortfall,” he said. He identified power, transportation and healthcare among the critical sectors expected to benefit from the proposed financing. “These funds will primarily be directed towards critical infrastructure projects in various sectors, including power, transportation and healthcare, amongst others,” the president said. Tinubu maintained that prompt consideration of the request would enable the government meet its obligations to Nigerians through timely disbursement of funds and effective execution of the projects. He said: “Given the urgent nature of these needs and the importance of stabilising the country, it is crucial to seek the consideration and approval of the National Assembly leadership and the entire National Assembly for the 2026–2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan.” The President, who noted that legislative approval will enable government proceed with the proposed interventions, said: “This will enable the government to fulfil its obligations to the Nigerian people through timely disbursements and effective project implementation.” The President of the Senate, thereafter, referred the communication to the Senate Committee on Local and Foreign Debts for further legislative action, to report at plenary within one week. The committee is expected to examine the proposal, potentially in collaboration with the Senate Committee on Appropriations and other relevant committees. The letter, as presented to the Senate, did not provide a detailed project-by-project breakdown of the proposed facilities, the specific financing terms or the amount earmarked for each sector. The letter, titled “Federal Government 2026-2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plans, read: “ I write in reference to the above subjects and to submit the attached federal government 2026-2027 supplementary external borrowing plans for consideration and early approval of the National Assembly to ensure prompt implementation of our projects. “The 2026-2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan cuts across all sectors with specific emphasis on infrastructure, agriculture, health, education, water supply, growth, security, and employment generation, as well as financial management reforms, amongst others. “The total facility for the projects and programmes under the Borrowing Growing Plan is $20,517,000,000 and €1,045,083,643 respectively and the summary of the breakdown is attached to this presents. “So, distinguished colleagues, in light of the removal of the critical reforms of my administration, the need to accelerate growth of the national economy provides support for the External Borrowing Plan, which amounts to $20,517,755,901, and €1,045,083,643. “I want to emphasise that the projects and programmes included in the Borrowing Plan were selected based on thorough technical and economic evaluation, as well as their anticipated contribution to the socio-economic development of the country. “These initiatives aim to generate employment, promote skilled acquisition, foster entrepreneurship, reduce poverty and enhance food security, all of which improves the livelihood of the Nigerian child. “The majority of these projects and programs will be implemented across all the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory. In light of the need for significant infrastructure investment in the country and the vast financial resources needed to address this gap, it has become essential to pursue broader external borrowings to close the financing shortfall. “These funds will primarily be directed towards critical infrastructure projects in various sectors, including power, transportation and healthcare, among others. “Given the urgent nature of these needs and the importance of stabilising the country, it is crucial to seek the consideration and approval of the National Assembly leadership and the entire National Assembly for the 2026-2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan. “This will enable the government fulfill its obligations to the Nigerian people through timely disbursements and effective project implementation. “This request will be looked at by the Committee on Local and Foreign Debts, probably in collaboration with the Preparation and Finance, but majorly by the Committee on Local and Foreign Debts. And you can report back in one week.” ₦269.4bn promissory notes Similarly, President Bola Tinubu asked the National Assembly to approve the establishment and expansion of the federal government’s Promissory Note Programme to settle outstanding verified liabilities totalling N269.44 billion. This was contained in a letter by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, SGF, Senator George Akume, which was read on the floor of the House at plenary in Abuja yesterday. The request is aimed at addressing outstanding contractual, project-related and other financial obligations owed various categories of creditors. In a letter dated August 18, 2026, and received by the Office of the Speaker on October 21, Akume said the liabilities amounted to N269,446,402,822.56, following a comprehensive review by relevant ministries, departments and agencies, MDAs. He said Tinubu had approved the proposal to establish and expand the programme as a mechanism for settling the verified obligations. According to the letter, the programme is designed to provide “a structured, transparent and fiscally responsible framework” for settling the outstanding debts, while ensuring that only verified and validated claims are admitted. The President is seeking legislative approval for the issuance of promissory notes worth N269.44 billion, or such other amount as may be approved by the National Assembly, to settle the liabilities contained in the accompanying schedule. The request also seeks approval for the inclusion of identified categories of liabilities and beneficiaries in the programme, subject to final verification, reconciliation and certification by the relevant government agencies. Tinubu further asked the National Assembly to authorise the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, in collaboration with the Debt Management Office and other relevant agencies, to take the necessary steps to implement the programme. Akume explained that the proposal was intended to mitigate the continued accumulation of interest, penalties and other financial costs associated with the outstanding obligations. He said the arrangement would also provide relief to affected creditors and strengthen confidence in the federal government’s commitment to honouring legitimate contractual and other obligations. The SGF noted that the federal government had previously used the Promissory Note Programme to settle inherited local debts and contractual obligations, following Federal Executive Council’s approval and subsequent National Assembly approval. He added that the proposed arrangement was expected to facilitate the orderly settlement of the liabilities without imposing an immediate and disproportionate cash-flow burden on the federal government. According to the letter, the programme will also support fiscal planning by spreading repayment obligations over an appropriate period, in line with prudent debt management principles. Akume urged the House to give the request urgent consideration, citing the magnitude and age of some of the outstanding liabilities and the possibility of further accumulation of interest and associated costs. He said early legislative approval would enable the Federal Government commence the necessary processes for issuing the promissory notes and bringing the affected liabilities to a close. The detailed schedule of the liabilities, including the relevant categories, beneficiaries, amounts and supporting documentation, was forwarded to the National Assembly for consideration. items.title: The Tehran opening
items.description: HELD amid the threat of a renewed US-Israeli attack on Iran and escalating conflict in the Arabian Peninsula, the meeting between Iranian leaders and members of the Makkah Defence Alliance was deeply significant — though it remained unclear whether the talks had produced any major breakthrough. The quadrilateral meeting reportedly discussed “regional cooperation, the US-Israeli aggression against Iran and its consequences”, among other topics. It was the first high-level contact between Iran and all of the alliance’s members since Saudi Arabia was drawn deeper into its conflict with the Houthis. The gathering came days after a brief visit to Tehran by Pakistan’s army chief, during which he reportedly proposed the meeting — a suggestion Iranian leaders responded to positively. That visit was essentially a part of Pakistan’s mediatory efforts to restart the stalled peace talks between America and Iran, and a response to the latest flare-up in the region. Since the collapse of a brief ceasefire reached in April, the United States has imposed an economic blockade on Iran in an attempt to force it to capitulate. It has not. Iran has kept control of the Strait of Hormuz, through which around a fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas used to flow. The diplomatic efforts of Pakistan and Qatar have so far failed to break the stalemate. The main stumbling block to resuming peace talks has been President Trump’s insistence that Iran give up its enriched uranium stockpile. Iran has refused, insisting that the US must end its naval blockade and start negotiations on the seven points that overlap with the Islamabad memorandum of understanding. Iranian leaders have repeatedly declared that “not a single particle of enriched nuclear material” would leave Iran. Regional peace can be ensured only through a regional security architecture. Tensions rose further with reports of a possible joint US-Israeli attack on Iran before the US midterm elections. According to American media, Israel had been pressing Trump to resume airstrikes before Israel’s own general elections, which were held yesterday. There are still indications that Trump could restart military action after the American midterms on Nov 3. Iranian officials warned last week that if Iran were attacked again, its forces would widen their targets to data centres and underwater internet cables in the region. The situation has grown more volatile with the escalation of the Saudi-Houthi conflict. The Yemeni rebel group, which now controls a large part of the country and Bab al-Mandeb, a critical chokepoint on the Red Sea, has repeatedly struck key Saudi installations. Against that backdrop, the visit by senior Saudi officials to Tehran stands out as a significant outreach at a time of profound tension between the two countries, with Saudi Arabia absorbing near-daily attacks by the Iran-backed Houthis. The kingdom was represented by Defence Minister Prince Khalid — the brother and trusted envoy of the crown prince. His decision to travel to Iran under such conditions signalled that the Saudi leadership wants to avert another round of hostilities between the US, Israel and Iran, which could bring Iranian retaliatory strikes on American interests and installations in Saudi Arabia while the kingdom is still battling the Houthis. For Iran, the presence of senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan has been symbolically important: Iranian officials are eager to sideline the US from regional security and diplomatic arrangements. Iran’s president expressed hope that the talks could help consolidate “regional unity and cohesion”. For all the positivity, the central question remains whether the meeting could bridge the gap and help prevent a new round of US-Israeli aggression against Iran and, more importantly, de-escalate the conflict between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis. No joint statement was issued, but individual comments since have been encouraging on the possibility of a broader regional security mechanism. Mohsen Rezaei, head of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, seemed satisfied after meeting officials from the three countries. “Very good discussions took place between us,” he told Iranian state television. “I feel that a new atmosphere is emerging in the region. … I sensed a very positive atmosphere in the discussions among the gentlemen.” Iranian officials are also hopeful that the meeting could be a prelude to further steps towards shaping “endogenous security — an issue that we have been insisting on for decades”. The four countries have “agreed to continue discussions to strengthen cooperation … including on regional peace and security”. Indeed, the Tehran meeting was the most significant development yet that could help de-escalate the regional conflict. But the major question remains whether such emerging cooperation can prevent a fresh American-Israeli attack on Iran. The reported reinforcement of American forces in the region, together with Israel’s continued genocidal war in Gaza and military action in Lebanon, poses the biggest threat to regional and global peace. The continued presence of American bases and troops in the Gulf countries has made their security far more vulnerable. Most concerning is the escalating Saudi-Houthi conflict, which could trigger a wider conflagration and draw other countries into it. Iran could certainly play an important role in reaching a truce. The escalation could also hand Israel an opportunity to blunt resistance to its expansionist designs. Given Trump’s threatening rhetoric, there is a strong possibility that he will resume attacks on Iran after the midterm elections; the one thing that could stop him is the Republicans losing their majority in both the House and the Senate. And whatever the outcome of the Israeli general elections, there is no indication that the defeat of Netanyahu would change the policy of the Zionist state in any significant way. The divisions among regional countries give Israel complete impunity. The quadrilateral meeting in Tehran and Iran’s positive response are certainly good omens. But the sources of tension remain that will not be easy to resolve, and the gap has yet to be bridged. It is vital that the Gulf countries refuse to let their soil be used for American aggression. Regional security can be ensured only through a regional security architecture. The Tehran meeting has provided an important opening for any such cooperation. The writer is an author and journalist. zhussain100@yahoo.com X: @hidhussain Published in Dawn, October 28th, 2026

items.title: Oil prices rise after attack on Saudi Arabian refinery reignites supply concerns
items.description: Oil prices rose on Wednesday after an attack on a refinery in Saudi Arabia, the ​world’s biggest crude exporter, renewed concerns around the ‌risks to supply in the Middle East stemming from the conflict with Iran and its proxies. Brent crude futures rose $1.48, or 1.3%, to $115.36 a ​barrel as of 0140 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate ​crude rose $1.22, or 1.22%, to $101.12. Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis said on Tuesday ⁠they had hit Saudi Arabia’s biggest oil refinery with ​a missile, intensifying their strikes against the world’s second-largest crude ​producer. Saudi authorities did not immediately confirm the strike on the 550,000-barrel-per-day facility. Prices swung back after dropping nearly $2 on Tuesday as talks in the Middle East eased supply worries. That was despite data expected to show a rise in crude inventories ‌in ⁠the US. Crude oil stockpiles rose about 15,000 barrels in the week ended October 23, according to a Reuters poll of eight analysts. The OPEC+ oil-producing countries are expected to keep their ​December output targets steady on Sunday, three people with knowledge of the matter told Reuters, in line with market expectations. Production in most of the ​seven core ⁠OPEC+ members — Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan and Oman — is below their output targets. Crude oil exports from Russia’s Baltic and Black Sea ports could fall next month as domestic refiners increase diesel output after a deal with Washington this month, traders said.

items.title: Affaire Epstein : de nouvelles accusations relancent la controverse autour de Donald Trump
items.description: À huit jours des élections de mi-mandat aux États-Unis, des élus démocrates demandent la nomination d’un procureur spécial chargé d’examiner les liens passés entre Donald Trump et Jeffrey Epstein. Ils s’appuient sur un rapport évoquant les témoignages de onze femmes, dont cinq accusent directement le président américain de viols ou d’agressions sexuelles. La Maison-Blanche rejette fermement ces accusations. Des élus démocrates du Congrès américain ont réclamé, lundi 26 octobre, la désignation d’un procureur spécial pour enquêter sur les liens entre Donald Trump et Jeffrey Epstein, financier condamné pour des crimes sexuels et retrouvé mort en prison en 2019. Cette demande intervient à huit jours des élections de mi-mandat, alors que l’affaire continue de peser sur le débat politique américain. La requête émane de membres démocrates de la commission judiciaire de la Chambre des représentants. Ses auteurs reconnaissent toutefois que leur initiative a peu de chances d’aboutir. La nomination d’un procureur spécial relève du ministre de la Justice, Todd Blanche, ancien avocat personnel de Donald Trump. Pour justifier leur demande, les élus démocrates s’appuient sur un rapport publié lundi, fondé sur les témoignages de onze femmes. Selon ce document, cinq d’entre elles ont directement accusé Donald Trump de les avoir violées ou agressées sexuellement en compagnie ou en présence de Jeffrey Epstein. Ces accusations sont contestées et ne constituent pas, à elles seules, une preuve de culpabilité. Donald Trump a toujours affirmé avoir rompu ses relations avec Epstein bien avant que ce dernier ne fasse l’objet de poursuites judiciaires. Il assure également n’avoir rien su des crimes sexuels du financier. Dans un communiqué, Jamie Raskin, principal représentant démocrate au sein de la commission judiciaire, accuse le ministère de la Justice de chercher à protéger le président. « Le ministère de la Justice de Trump semble dissimuler ces crimes pour protéger le président », affirme-t-il. Les élus démocrates mettent également en cause l’indépendance de Todd Blanche, estimant que ses anciennes fonctions d’avocat personnel de Donald Trump soulèvent des questions sur sa capacité à agir dans ce dossier. La Maison-Blanche dénonce des accusations « ridicules » La Maison-Blanche a vivement réagi à ces accusations. Sur le réseau social X, son directeur de la communication, Steven Cheung, a qualifié les allégations de « connerie totale ». Il a accusé les démocrates et les médias de relancer des accusations contre le président à l’approche de chaque scrutin, assurant que les Américains n’étaient « pas dupes ». L’affaire Epstein constitue néanmoins un sujet politiquement sensible pour Donald Trump, notamment auprès d’une partie de sa base MAGA, où les interrogations sur les circonstances de la mort du financier ont alimenté différentes théories du complot. Selon les médias américains, les démocrates ont consacré plus de 35 millions de dollars à des publicités de campagne spécifiquement axées sur cette affaire. La publication des dossiers Epstein toujours contestée Le ministère américain de la Justice a publié, le 30 janvier, plus de trois millions de pages liées au dossier Epstein. L’administration Trump affirme ainsi avoir rempli ses obligations au titre d’une loi adoptée par le Congrès en novembre, destinée à faire la lumière sur cette affaire. Toutefois, des parlementaires démocrates, mais aussi républicains, ont dénoncé la rétention présumée de certaines informations et le maintien de nombreuses parties caviardées dans les documents rendus publics. La révélation des relations passées entre Jeffrey Epstein et différentes personnalités a déjà provoqué des enquêtes, des arrestations et des démissions, principalement en Europe. Il convient toutefois de rappeler qu’une personne peut être mentionnée dans les documents liés à Epstein sans avoir commis d’acte répréhensible. La nature des liens entretenus avec le financier et les éventuelles responsabilités individuelles doivent être examinées au cas par cas.
