items.title: Dangote refinery IPO draws three times target demand, sources say
items.description: Nigeria’s $1.6 billion Dangote refinery initial ‌public offering has drawn about three times the total targeted orders, two people with knowledge of the situation said, underscoring strong demand for what has been billed as “The People’s IPO”. The share sale, which closes on Tuesday, has about 6.4 trillion naira ($4.78 billion) in orders from Nigerian retail and institutional investors, one person involved told Reuters. Aliko Dangote, the billionaire owner of the Lagos refinery, said the sale is targeting millions of ordinary Nigerians and Africans who can buy shares for as little as $4. The order book is expected to grow once subscriptions from investors in other African countries are included, one of the people said, adding that Dangote has received subscriptions from more than 2 million investors through digital channels so far. Given the demand, Dangote was expected to exercise a greenshoe option that would allow it to increase the offering size to as much as $2.1 billion, the person added. A ⁠Dangote spokesperson declined to comment on the demand and possibility of exercising the greenshoe option. The IPO comes as Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals FZE has benefited from stronger margins, with higher crude oil prices linked to the Iran war lifting earnings. The refinery, which began commercial operations in early 2024, has steadily increased output and expanded exports, including shipments of jet fuel to Europe and other African markets, helping position Nigeria as a potential net exporter of refined petroleum products. Share allocation will begin ​next week ⁠ahead of the stock’s planned listing on the Nigerian Exchange later in November, the company’s IPO prospectus said. Built at a cost of about $20 billion, the refinery has transformed Nigeria’s fuel ⁠market since ​it began operating. It processes about 700,000 barrels of ​crude oil per day and aims to double capacity to 1.4 million barrels per day by 2029.

items.title: Regional security
items.description: THE fact that high officials from the Makkah defence pact partner states — Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye — were in Tehran on Monday made global headlines, and with good reason. At a time when the clouds of war are once again hovering over the Gulf, the meeting sent a strong message that regional states with often competing agendas can come together and discuss their issues at the negotiating table. The event was also significant as the Makkah alliance has been seen as an alternative defence arrangement vis-à-vis Iran’s ‘Axis of Resistance’. Pakistan was represented by the chief of defence forces, while significantly, Saudi Arabia sent its defence minister, a brother of the crown prince. This shows that Riyadh accorded the highest priority to the meeting. The official Iranian readout said the participants pledged to “continue the dialogue … for peace and security in the region.” The event is also further proof of Pakistan’s constructive efforts in the diplomatic arena, as the meet-up was held after the CDF — who was in Tehran last week — suggested it. All regional states are wary of possible fresh US/Israeli attacks on Iran, and the Tehran meeting must be seen in this framework. Moreover, Saudi Arabia has likely reached out to Iran to get the Islamic Republic to use its connections with Yemen’s Houthi Ansarallah group to stop its attacks on the kingdom. Riyadh is also concerned about Iranian retaliation in the face of a renewed Israeli and American attack. Perhaps Yemen can be the first area for the Makkah pact allies and Iran to discuss. A fresh push for peace should be made that envisages an immediate ceasefire supplemented by an end to Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, and a lifting of the Saudi-led blockade on Houthi-held areas in Yemen. Both Saudi Arabia and Iran, as well as other regional powers, should advocate a negotiated settlement to the Yemeni civil war. Beyond Yemen, the fact that the US and Israel are preparing for fresh aggression against Iran could spoil efforts for a regional entente. This is why all participants of the Tehran meeting must clearly say that they oppose attacks on Iran or any other regional state. Iran and the Makkah pact states should also pledge not to let external actors use their soil to launch aggression against each other. In fact, while inviting Iran to join the Makkah alliance may not be practical at this juncture, regional states can at least agree to a common non-aggression framework. That would send a powerful message to external actors that seek to destabilise the region. States of the region are making sincere efforts to prevent a return to war. It is time Washington and Tel Aviv read the writing on the wall and abandoned their destructive plans. Published in Dawn, October 28th, 2026

items.title: Burkina Faso : La Douane intercepte 2 310 bâtons de dynamite et 7 500 détonateurs
items.description: Ce mardi 27 octobre 2026, la Direction générale des Douanes du Burkina Faso a présenté une saisie majeure de matériel explosif réalisée lors de deux interventions ciblées. Au total, 2 310 bâtons de dynamite dissimulés dans un camion de transit et 7 500 détonateurs découverts à bord d'un bus de transport de voyageurs ont été neutralisés par les équipes douanières. Présentant ces substances hautement dangereuses, le Directeur général des Douanes, le Dr Yves Kafando, a fermement enjoint les contrebandiers de cesser leurs pratiques illégales, mettant en garde contre des sanctions rigoureuses et rappelant les menaces majeures que font peser ces trafics sur la sécurité des populations, la faune et l'environnement. La vigilance des douaniers a une nouvelle fois porté ses fruits. Ce mardi 27 octobre 2026, la Direction générale des Douanes a rendu publique l'interception d'une impressionnante cargaison d'explosifs et d'équipements de mise à feu. Les opérations, menées sur deux fronts distincts par les services des douanes, se sont soldées par la confiscation de 2 310 bâtons de dynamite d'une part, et de 7 500 détonateurs d'autre part. L'ingéniosité des fraudeurs a été mise en échec : les bâtons de dynamite étaient dissimulés au sein d'un camion de transit, tandis que la cargaison de détonateurs voyageait clandestinement à bord d'un bus de transport commun de passagers. Lors de la présentation de cette saisie, le Directeur général des Douanes, le Dr Yves Kafando, n'a pas caché son inquiétude face à la nature et à la quantité des produits confisqués, qu'il a formellement qualifiés de « très nocifs ». Le responsable de l'administration douanière a tenu à alerter l'opinion sur les conséquences graves que pourrait engendrer la circulation incontrôlée de telles matières. Selon lui, au-delà du risque direct et immédiat pour la vie des citoyens, ces substances explosives représentent une menace environnementale majeure, capable d'endommager les écosystèmes et de porter atteinte à la faune. Face à la persistance de la contrebande de produits dangereux, la Direction générale des Douanes réaffirme sa détermination. Le Dr Yves Kafando a lancé un appel pressant aux fraudeurs et aux trafiquants afin qu'ils mettent fin à leurs activités criminelles. Avertissant que les contrevenants s'exposent désormais à toute la rigueur des sanctions réglementaires et pénales, le patron des douanes a réaffirmé l'engagement de ses services à renforcer les contrôles pour garantir la sécurité du territoire et la protection des populations. items.title: Burkina Faso : Le gouvernement interdit toute nouvelle mobilisation de terres aux promoteurs immobiliers
items.description: À travers un communiqué officiel daté du 27 octobre 2026, le Ministère de la Construction de la Patrie a ordonné l'arrêt immédiat de toute mobilisation foncière à des fins d'aménagement par les promoteurs immobiliers agréés et ex-promoteurs sur l'ensemble du territoire burkinabè. S'appuyant sur la loi n°008-2023/ALT du 20 juin 2023 relative à la promotion immobilière, l'exécutif interdit également la proposition de sites aux collectivités territoriales pour des opérations de lotissement ou d'apurement du passif foncier. Désormais, tout projet de valorisation de terrains déjà acquis doit repasser sous l'arbitrage exclusif du ministère, sous peine de lourdes sanctions réglementaires et judiciaires. La régulation foncière franchit une étape décisive au Burkina Faso. Par le biais du communiqué officiel n°2026_005/MCP/SG/SGA, signé par le Secrétaire général adjoint Yacouba Siko pour le compte du Ministre de la Construction de la Patrie, les autorités réaffirment l'application rigoureuse du cadre légal. En vertu des dispositions de la loi n°008-2023/ALT du 20 juin 2023 portant promotion immobilière, il est désormais formellement interdit à tout promoteur immobilier agréé, ainsi qu'à tout ex-promoteur, de mobiliser du foncier dans le but de réaliser la moindre forme d'aménagement. De surcroît, le texte proscrit catégoriquement la mise à disposition de sites auprès des structures ou collectivités territoriales en vue de mener des opérations de lotissement ou d'apurement du passif foncier. Afin d'encadrer la politique du logement et de veiller à une planification urbaine cohérente, l'État impose un contrôle direct sur les terrains existants. Les promoteurs et anciens promoteurs disposant déjà de parcelles mobilisées avant la diffusion de cet acte officiel, et souhaitant s'associer aux efforts publics de construction de logements au profit des populations, doivent s'adresser exclusivement au ministre de la Construction de la Patrie. Il reviendra à l'autorité ministérielle d'évaluer la faisabilité et la conformité du foncier au regard des textes de loi et des orientations de l'urbanisme. Afin d'assurer le respect strict de cette directive, le ministère rappelle l'existence de verrous juridiques dissuasifs. Tout promoteur immobilier s'adonnant à des mobilisations illégales de terres, tout comme toute collectivité territoriale coupable d'association ou de complicité avec des promoteurs agréés ou ex-promoteurs, s'exposeront à la rigueur des sanctions prévues par les lois en vigueur. En appelant au sens élevé des responsabilités de l'ensemble des acteurs de la chaîne foncière, le gouvernement entend assainir définitivement le secteur immobilier national. items.title: Guet-apens mortel à Bobo-Dioulasso : Sayouba Sankara et Boukary Kabor, assassins de Daouda Traoré condamnés à la réclusion criminelle à perpétuité
items.description: Le tribunal a rendu son verdict le 26 octobre 2026 dans le procès opposant le ministère public à Sayouba Sankara et Boukary Kaboré, poursuivis pour l'assassinat de Daouda Traoré. Condamnés à la réclusion criminelle à perpétuité, conformément aux réquisitions du procureur, les deux hommes passeront le reste de leur vie en prison. Ce jugement met un terme à une affaire criminelle particulièrement odieuse remontant au 26 mars 2025 au secteur n°2 (Médina-Coura) à Bobo-Dioulasso, où la victiame avait été attirée dans un guet-apens sous couvert d'une transaction automobile. Après avoir reconnu devant les juges leur intention de « limer » la victime, les deux complices avaient abandonné sa dépouille au cimetière du secteur n°17 avant d'incendier sa motocyclette sur la route de Ouagadougou. La décision de la justice est tombée avec une fermeté catégorique. Le 26 octobre 2026, le tribunal a condamné Sayouba Sankara et Kaboré Boukary à la réclusion criminelle à perpétuité pour l'assassinat de Daouda Traoré. En infligeant la peine maximale aux deux accusés, les juges ont suivi à la lettre le réquisitoire du ministère public, qui avait demandé que les deux hommes passent le reste de leur existence derrière les barreaux en raison de la gravité exceptionnelle des faits. L'affaire prend sa source le 26 mars 2025 dans le secteur n°2 (Médina-Coura) de Bobo-Dioulasso. Ce jour-là, Daouda Traoré se rend à moto au bureau de Sayouba Sankara, un vendeur de véhicules auprès duquel il devait finaliser l'achat d'une voiture en lui remettant la somme convenue. Mais la transaction commerciale tourne au piège mortel : l'acheteur ne ressortira jamais vivant du bureau. Avec la complicité de Boukary Kaboré, un homme en tenue, Sayouba Sankara assassine froidement sa victime. Dans la nuit qui suit le crime, les deux hommes transportent et dissimulent le corps au cimetière du secteur n°17, avant de conduire la motocyclette de Daouda Traoré à la sortie de Bobo-Dioulasso, sur la route de Ouagadougou, pour y mettre le feu. Initialement programmé pour le 8 juin 2026, le procès avait été ajourné à plusieurs reprises en raison des exigences des prévenus. Sayouba Sankara et Boukary Kaboré réclamaient l'assistance d'un avocat avant de s'expliquer sur le déroulement des faits. Une fois le défenseur désigné par l'État, les débats se sont ouverts le 12 octobre 2026 devant le tribunal. À la barre, les deux accusés ont fini par passer aux aveux complets, reconnaissant avoir agi de concert pour « limer » leur victime — une expression dont ils ont eux-mêmes précisé le sens aux juges en admettant qu'il s'agissait d'éliminer physiquement Daouda Traoré. Face à ces révélations et au caractère odieux du crime, le parquet a requis la prison à vie, réquisition intégralement entérinée par le jugement final. L’article Guet-apens mortel à Bobo-Dioulasso : Sayouba Sankara et Boukary Kabor, assassins de Daouda Traoré condamnés à la réclusion criminelle à perpétuité est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Pratique de l’excision à Kaya: « 2 500 FCFA et une boule de savon par enfant », les aveux glaçants d’une prévenue
items.description: Selon les informations rapportées par le média MoussoNews , le Tribunal de grande instance (TGI) de Kaya a ouvert, le lundi 26 octobre 2026 à la mairie de Boussouma, une audience foraine de trois jours organisée en partenariat avec l'ONG ENABEL. Au cœur de ce procès de grande ampleur figurent 39 prévenus — dont 38 femmes et un homme — poursuivis pour la pratique et la complicité d'excision sur une trentaine de fillettes âgées de 4 à 6 ans. Première accusée appelée à la barre, T.K., une sexagénaire déplacée interne, a livré un témoignage troublant sur une activité clandestine pratiquée depuis une quinzaine d'années et tarifée 2 500 FCFA assortis d'une boule de savon par enfant. La salle des fêtes de la mairie de Boussouma sert de cadre à un procès emblématique. Dans le cadre d'une audience foraine soutenue par l'ONG ENABEL, le Tribunal de grande instance (TGI) de Kaya s'est délocalisé pour examiner un lourd dossier de mutilations génitales féminines (MGF). Comme le relate le journal MoussoNews , pas moins de 39 prévenus doivent répondre devant les juges de faits d'excision perpétrés sur une trentaine de jeunes victimes âgées de seulement 4 à 6 ans. L'organisation de ces audiences délocalisées vise autant à réprimer des atteintes graves à la santé des enfants qu'à sensibiliser l'opinion publique au plus près des réalités du terrain. Première à comparaitre à la barre, T.K., une femme de soixante ans domiciliée à Kaya, a détaillé sans détour son mode opératoire. Originaire d'un village natal qu'elle a quitté en raison de la crise sécuritaire pour rejoindre Kaya avec d'autres personnes déplacées internes, cette dernière pratiquait l'excision depuis plus de quinze ans. Héritière d'un savoir-faire familial transmis par sa mère — elle-même exciseuse —, elle a reconnu opérer pendant un mois chaque année, à raison d'une vingtaine de fillettes par jour. Pour chaque intervention, réalisée au moyen d'une simple lame de rasoir sans gants de protection, les parents lui versaient 2 500 FCFA et une boule de savon, générant des gains journaliers évalués par le tribunal à près de 50 000 FCFA. Interrogée sur la portée pénale de ses actes, la prévenue a soutenu devant le tribunal qu'elle ignorait l'interdiction légale de l'excision au Burkina Faso. Une ligne de défense vivement réfutée par le ministère public, qui a mis en lumière le caractère dissimulé de l'activité en lui demandant pourquoi elle n'avait jamais apposé de pancarte publicitaire devant son domicile si la pratique était licite. Pour justifier la guérison des plaies en quinze ans d'exercice, T.K. a affirmé recourir à des incantations traditionnelles, avant de multiplier les demandes de pardon et de solliciter la clémence des juges. L'examen du dossier se poursuit à Boussouma pour déterminer le niveau d'implication des 38 autres coprévenus. items.title: Bobo-Dioulasso : Il verse 1,5 million de FCFA à des individus pour assassiner son frère, la victime échappe à la mort
items.description: « Je leur ai simplement demandé d’aller l’effrayer pour qu’il quitte le lieu de travail », a déclaré Sahilé devant la chambre criminelle du Tribunal de grande instance (TGI) de Bobo-Dioulasso, le lundi 26 octobre 2026. Sahilé, un jeune orpailleur de 30 ans, vivant en union libre et père de six enfants, comparaissait devant cette juridiction pour répondre des faits d’incitation à la commission d’un crime d’assassinat. Il est accusé d’avoir sollicité des individus pour s’en prendre à son petit frère, avec lequel il était en conflit. Les faits Selon les éléments présentés à l’audience, à la suite d’une dispute familiale, Sahilé aurait contacté des individus depuis Séguéla, en République de Côte d’Ivoire, afin qu’ils ôtent la vie à son petit frère de même père, en échange d’une somme de 1 500 000 FCFA. La victime a toutefois échappé à la mort grâce à l’intervention d’un passant. Un passant sauve la victime D’après les débats, l’un des individus contactés par Sahilé, nommé Gnanmôgô, aurait mobilisé d’autres personnes pour passer à l’acte. La victime aurait alors été violemment agressée à coups d’arme blanche. Un passant est finalement intervenu et l’a transportée à l’hôpital, lui permettant ainsi d’échapper à la mort. Un conflit autour d’un site d’orpaillage À la barre, Sahilé a expliqué que le différend avec son petit frère était lié à leurs activités d’orpaillage. Il affirme avoir travaillé pendant plusieurs années sur un site avant de partir seul à Séguéla, où il a poursuivi ses activités pendant neuf mois. Lorsque le site a commencé à produire de l’or, leur grand frère aurait demandé à ce que le cadet rejoigne Sahilé afin qu’ils travaillent ensemble. Une décision à laquelle l’accusé dit s’être opposé. Malgré son refus, son petit frère a finalement rejoint le site sur instruction de leur aîné. C’est dans ce contexte de tensions que Sahilé aurait pris contact avec des individus pour s’en prendre à son cadet. Selon les éléments évoqués à l’audience, les personnes sollicitées auraient initialement demandé 500 000 FCFA pour exécuter la mission. L’accusé aurait ensuite ajouté un million de FCFA, portant le montant total à 1 500 000 FCFA. Sahilé nie avoir voulu tuer son frère Interrogé sur ses intentions, l’accusé a contesté avoir commandité un assassinat. Il soutient qu’il voulait uniquement faire peur à son petit frère afin de le pousser à quitter le site d’orpaillage. « Je leur ai simplement demandé d’aller l’effrayer pour qu’il quitte le lieu de travail », a-t-il insisté. Le juge lui a alors demandé : — N’était-ce pas pour mettre réellement fin à la vie de ton frère que tu as ajouté un million de FCFA ? — Non, j’avais bien précisé que je voulais simplement qu’ils aillent l’effrayer pour qu’il quitte les lieux du travail, a répondu Sahilé. Le magistrat a poursuivi : — Si c’était réellement pour l’effrayer seulement, aurais-tu déboursé 1 500 000 FCFA ? — Non, mais je n’avais aucune intention malveillante, a rétorqué l’accusé. Interrogé par le parquet sur son parcours, Sahilé a indiqué qu’il s’était rendu en Côte d’Ivoire en 2013 pour travailler avec son grand frère. Des accusations supplémentaires évoquées à l’audience Au cours des débats, le juge a également évoqué des faits qui se seraient produits après l’agression. Selon les éléments présentés, alors qu’il se trouvait au chevet de son petit frère à l’hôpital, Sahilé aurait continué à contacter un marabout connu sous le nom de Kadhafi, dans le but de s’en prendre mystiquement à certains membres de sa famille, qui souhaitaient porter l’affaire devant la justice. L’accusé a de nouveau contesté cette version. Il a affirmé avoir contacté le marabout dans le but de faire taire les membres de sa famille pour qu’ils ne parlent pas de l’affaire. Prenant la parole, l’avocat de la partie civile a rappelé la proximité qui existait entre Sahilé et la victime. Selon lui, les deux frères entretenaient de bonnes relations et allaient jusqu’à échanger leurs T-shirts. L’avocat a déploré que, malgré cette complicité, l’accusé soit soupçonné d’avoir voulu faire tuer son propre frère. Il a également soutenu que Sahilé, alors qu’il faisait semblant de rester auprès de la victime à l’hôpital, cherchait encore des moyens de s’en prendre à leur grand frère et à d’autres membres de la famille. L’avocat de la partie civile a par ailleurs affirmé que le bras droit de l’aîné de l’accusé avait été paralysé. Ces éléments ont été évoqués dans le cadre des débats à l’audience. La partie civile réclame 8 millions de FCFA Au regard des conséquences de l’agression et des dépenses médicales que la victime continuerait de supporter, l’avocat de la partie civile a réclamé la somme de 8 000 000 FCFA à titre de réparation. De son côté, l’avocat de la défense a évoqué le dilemme auquel son client aurait été confronté, tout en reconnaissant que la morale pouvait également entrer en ligne de compte. Pour défendre Sahilé, il a fait référence à une citation attribuée à Laurent Gbagbo : « Quand on t’envoie, il faut savoir t’envoyer. » Selon lui, son client avait demandé aux individus sollicités d’effrayer son frère, mais ces derniers auraient choisi d’aller au-delà des instructions reçues. Le parquet requiert 30 ans de prison ferme Dans ses réquisitions, le ministère public a demandé à la chambre criminelle de déclarer Sahilé coupable des faits d’incitation à la commission d’un crime d’assassinat. Pour le parquet, les éléments du dossier constituent des preuves suffisantes pour établir sa culpabilité. Au titre de la peine, le ministère public a requis 30 ans d’emprisonnement ferme contre l’accusé. Invité à prendre la parole en dernier, Sahilé a présenté ses excuses au tribunal, à l’assistance ainsi qu’aux membres de sa famille. Il a déclaré regretter ses actes. À l’issue de l’audience, le tribunal a mis l’affaire en délibéré au 9 novembre 2026. #tiwana24 Justice Infos Burkina L’article Bobo-Dioulasso : Il verse 1,5 million de FCFA à des individus pour assassiner son frère, la victime échappe à la mort est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Brazil: New Evidence of Serious Police Misconduct in Deadly Raid
items.description: Play Video Read a text description of this video TEXT ON SCREEN October 28, 2025 Rio de Janeiro, Brazil NARRATION On the morning of October 28th, 2025, hundreds of police officers surrounded two low-income neighborhoods in Rio de Janeiro. By nightfall, the operation would become the deadliest in Brazil's history. TEXT ON SCREEN WARNING. This video contains graphic content, including blurred images of dead bodies. Viewer discretion advised. NARRATION 122 people were killed, including two children and five police officers. According to the autopsy records, over eighty five percent of non-police victims were Black. Police in Rio de Janeiro are required by Supreme Court order to wear body cameras. However, only twenty-three percent of officers wore body cameras that day, and in the footage reviewed by Human Rights Watch, not a single killing was captured on camera. LOWER THIRD Damir Khairat Research Technologist Digital Investigations Lab NARRATION Human Rights Watch was given access to the prosecutor's investigation into the operation, including 8,800 pages of records, 122 autopsies, and nearly 4,000 hours of body camera footage. TEXT ON SCREEN Prosecutors have released the body camera footage shown in this video. Most footage is sealed as evidence and cannot be published. NARRATION Watching all the footage day and night without any breaks would have taken a single researcher almost six months. So, we trained several artificial intelligence models to help us identify the moments that mattered most. First, we needed to organize everything. The models, alongside software that Human Rights Watch developed, synchronized recordings from different officers, mapped their locations, and scanned footage for gunshots and signs of camera tampering. From there we had a searchable platform that let us view the operation as one coordinated event, rather than thousands of separate recordings. What we found was evidence of widespread tampering and obstruction of body cameras. And it consistently happened at the exact moment cameras should have been recording, during arrests, shootouts, or while officers entered homes. Authorities said that the purpose of the raid was to arrest suspected drug traffickers. The evidence we found points to an operation that appeared lethal by design. To explain how we came to this conclusion, let's look at some examples of the moments we trained our AI models to detect. An officer's camera captured this video in an alleyway as a large group of his colleagues pass by, after which the officer quickly covers his camera. He or another officer then flags that there's a camera recording. SOUNDBITE [IN PORTUGUESE] The team has a camera. The team has a camera. No, no I’m talking about the thing there. NARRATION It's unclear why he covered it, but prosecutors later charged him with camera tampering. SOUNDBITE So, this would be the kind of like overall operational view. NARRATION To find incidents like this across almost 4,000 hours of footage from nearly 500 officers, we trained a model to detect similar moments when a camera continued recording, but the lens was covered. Here, an officer is seen struggling to pick the lock on the door of someone's home. Once it's open, he removes his camera and leaves it unattended for over an hour, presumably while he's inside the home. Because the camera was still capturing an image, this recording wasn't initially flagged by our software. So, we trained a second model to identify "stale scenes" where the recording stays the same for long periods of time. As our models learned and improved, they uncovered lots of suspicious recording gaps. In the end, we documented more than 250 camera obstructions. Moments like these are exactly the situations that body cameras are meant to document, helping ensure that any unlawful behavior is captured and that circumstances surrounding the 122 killings can be properly investigated. Another method we used was an AI system that analyzes audio to detect gunshots. After we trained it specifically for Rio police body cameras and local conditions, the model successfully detected most gunshots in a test set of videos. We were also able to use AI to pull text directly from the videos, like the date, time, location and ID number of the officer wearing the camera. But one of the most striking findings came from what we didn't see. Despite the scale of the operation and the number of deaths, we found no footage showing the killings themselves. NARRATION To understand what was missing, we organized body camera recordings across the operation using extracted timestamps. TEXT ON SCREEN Unusable footage Usable footage NARRATION We found that more than half the officers’ recordings had either ended or had significant gaps by noon. From there, the usable footage continued to decline, just as the operation became most deadly. The missing footage, combined with extensive evidence of camera tampering, suggests that body cameras were deliberately misused to prevent killings from being recorded. Throughout our investigation, AI was one tool out of many. Our team of researchers interviewed witnesses in Rio, visited the neighborhood where the killings took place, analyzed police records and autopsies, verified photographs and videos, and manually reviewed AI findings. What AI provided was speed and scale. It helped us process thousands of hours of footage, connect pieces of evidence, and focus our attention where it mattered most. In other words, AI helped us find needles in a very large haystack. Now, it's up to Brazilian prosecutors to thoroughly investigate both the killings and the decisions that led to such a deadly operation. Those who use disproportionate force or misuse body cameras should be held accountable. To learn more about the events of October 28th and Human Rights Watch’s findings, visit HRW.org and read our investigation, A Strategy of Death. Police officers tampered with body cameras and was responsible for serious investigative failures during an operation ostensibly to arrest gang members in a low-income neighborhood in Rio de Janeiro on October 28, 2025. A year-long Human Rights Watch investigation concluded that police breached Supreme Court orders and their own protocols during Operation Containment, which appeared to be lethal by design. Federal and state prosecutors should initiate criminal and civil proceedings to investigate those responsible for abuses, including senior officials and police commanders. (Rio de Janeiro, October 28, 2026) – Police officers tampered with body cameras and failed to take crucial investigative steps during an operation in a low-income neighborhood in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, on October 28, 2025, Human Rights Watch said in an investigation published today. Evidence indicates police used excessive force and may have intentionally killed scores of men and boys. The investigation, “‘A Strategy of Death’: Investigating Brazil’s Deadliest Police Operation,” documents Operation Containment (Operação Contenção), in which a total of 122 people were killed. This included two children and four police officers killed that day, and a fifth police officer who later succumbed to his wounds. An additional two men were killed in the early morning before the official start of the operation. Eighty-five percent of non-police victims of the October 2025 raid were Black. “A Strategy of Death” Investigating Brazil’s Deadliest Police Operation Read the full investigation here None of the killings were captured in the thousands of hours of body camera footage sent by Rio de Janeiro Military Police to the Public Defender’s Office, which Human Rights Watch reviewed after being granted access. “Human Rights Watch processed thousands of hours of body camera footage and analyzed videos, official investigation files, and autopsy records for every victim, yet crucial questions remain because police failed to properly record killings, preserve crime scenes, or collect crucial data,” said Sophia Jones, open source researcher with the Digital Investigations Lab at Human Rights Watch. “The families of those killed, including police officers, deserve answers and accountability with a thorough, independent investigation.” Human Rights Watch interviewed 41 witnesses, family members, and experts, and analyzed 4,400 hours of body camera footage, 9,000 pages of official investigation files, 122 autopsy reports, court records, and hundreds of videos and photographs. Human Rights Watch analyzed the data using several machine learning models built in-house, followed by manual review and assessment by researchers. Based on Human Rights Watch analysis of data from Rio-based security research lab GENI (Grupo de Estudos dos Novos Ilegalismos or Group for the Study of New Illegalities), nongovernmental think tank Fórum Brasileiro de Segurança Pública (Brazilian Public Security Forum), independent security monitoring organization Fogo Cruzado (Crossfire), and media reports, Operation Containment was the deadliest documented one-day police operation in a country where police forces kill more than 6,000 people per year. Human Rights Watch visited the Complexo da Penha, the site of the operation, six months after the raid and found that the criminal group Red Command (Comando Vermelho)—the target of the operation—continued to impose its rule on residents. Despite the stated goal of carrying out 100 arrest warrants for alleged Red Command members, police records show they arrested only 17 of those for whom they had warrants, although it is not clear whether those are the warrants that justified the operation or other pending warrants. Police did not enter the home of the local Red Command leader, for whom they had a warrant, a Civil Police commander told prosecutors, even though body camera footage shows police moving around it. Despite a state law and a Supreme Court order mandating that police wear body cameras, only about 23 percent of the 2,500 civil and military police officers who participated in the raid did, the Rio de Janeiro government said. Machine-Enabled Forensics How Human Rights Watch used Artificial Intelligence to Analyze Body Camera Footage from Rio’s Deadliest Police Raid Read the methodology here Human Rights Watch analysis of the footage of the 527 military police officers who wore the cameras found widespread tampering and obstruction of their use. Officers left cameras running before the operation, effectively draining batteries; covered lenses; placed cameras where they would not capture officers’ actions; and left cameras in vehicles. Such tampering consistently occurred at key moments, during arrests, shootouts, or while officers entered homes, researchers found. Most tampering was on cameras worn by officers whose units engaged in frontline operations, such as the Battalion of Special Police Operations of the Military Police, the unit deployed to the forested area where the majority of killings took place. Researchers determined that 36 percent of gunshot clusters heard on their cameras occurred when the cameras were obstructed. Body camera footage showed officers assaulting and threatening to kill detainees, including a child, whom they forced to lie down next to a dead body while photographing him. In another recording, an officer tells officers to shoot detainees in the legs if they ran. In a third clip, an officer expressed frustration that body cameras prevented them from killing suspects. Researchers also analyzed or verified hundreds of videos and photographs taken by members of the local community that day. In one series of verified videos, officers pile dead bodies, some with their genitalia exposed, into an armored police vehicle, while joking. “Look how wonderful,” one officer said. “We like this.” While police said they spent months planning the operation, there was no evidence that they made any advance preparations to protect crime scenes and conduct forensic analysis. In addition, Civil Police failed to collect basic information for all but two of the 117 non-police victims, such as the names of police officers and residents who brought some of them to a hospital. Only seven suspects were taken to a hospital and subsequently arrested, compared with 117 people killed by police. That unusually high ratio of people killed to people injured (17 to 1) raises serious questions about whether police prioritized lethal force over arresting suspects. An analysis of victim autopsy reports also points in that direction. Over 40 percent of non-police victims in the reports analyzed were shot in the head, over 60 percent were shot four or more times, and nearly 75 percent were shot at least once on the back. One man was shot and then decapitated. According to forensic experts from the Independent Forensic Expert Group of the International Rehabilitation Council for Torture Victims consulted by Human Rights Watch, the evidence suggests that many were targeted and killed intentionally. In many instances, the trajectory of gunshot wounds was from bottom to top, which can be indicative of execution, such as when an individual is shot while lying down or otherwise incapacitated. Brazilian authorities should ensure a thorough and independent investigation into the planning and decisions by senior officials and police commanders that led to the deadly operation. Rio de Janeiro’s new governor, who will take office on January 6, 2027, should introduce a bill to separate forensic services from the Civil Police. “Our investigation shows police flouted the law and their own protocols during the disastrous raid,” said César Muñoz, Brazil director at Human Rights Watch. “Abusive police practices undermine public security by making communities less willing to collaborate with police, while fueling a cycle of violence that endangers both residents and police officers. Brazil needs new effective public security strategies that uphold human rights.”

items.title: Gaoua: 12 présumés escrocs de nationalité béninoise interpellés
items.description: Douze présumés escrocs de nationalité béninoise ont été interpellés les 21 et 22 octobre 2026 à Gaoua par le Service régional de la police judiciaire (SRPJ) du Djôrô. Ils sont soupçonnés d’avoir mis en place deux réseaux spécialisés dans l’escroquerie sous couvert de pratiques spirituelles, a annoncé mardi le chef du SRPJ, le capitaine de police Théophile Zongo. Selon le capitaine Zongo, l’enquête a été ouverte à la suite d’une plainte déposée le 21 octobre 2026 par un homme qui affirme avoir été escroqué de 185 000 FCFA par des individus se présentant comme des tradipraticiens. Ces derniers lui auraient réclamé 800 000 FCFA supplémentaires, sous peine de mort ou de devenir fou. Les investigations ont permis l’interpellation, le soir même, de trois suspects appartenant à un premier groupe. Grâce à la collaboration des populations, les enquêteurs ont ensuite identifié un second réseau opérant dans le quartier Tielkan. Neuf autres suspects ont été interpellés le 22 octobre. D’après la police, les deux groupes recrutaient des jeunes au Bénin pour les conduire au Burkina Faso, où ils étaient chargés de démarcher les populations dans les villages reculés et sur les sites d’orpaillage. Ils leur proposaient des bagues et des amulettes présentées comme des porte-bonheur, vendues entre 15 000 et 25 000 FCFA. Les victimes étaient ensuite orientées vers de prétendus maîtres spirituels qui leur prescrivaient des rituels de purification payants. Les sommes exigées pouvaient atteindre 800 000 FCFA. Des menaces de malheur, de maladie mentale ou de mort auraient également été proférées contre les personnes réticentes à payer. Le préjudice financier global n’est pas encore établi, a précisé le capitaine Zongo, ajoutant que plusieurs victimes ne se sont pas encore manifestées. Les investigations se poursuivent pour identifier d’éventuels complices. Les douze suspects seront présentés au procureur du Faso près le Tribunal de grande instance de Gaoua pour répondre des faits qui leur sont reprochés. La police nationale invite les populations à signaler tout comportement suspect aux numéros 16, 17 et 10-10. Agence d’Information du Burkina L’article Gaoua: 12 présumés escrocs de nationalité béninoise interpellés est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Vote-buying: High cost of politics is pricing out people with integrity – Inusah Fuseini
items.description: Former Tamale Central MP Inusah Fuseini says the growing cost of politics is pushing people with integrity out of public life and fuelling corruption. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Tuesday, he warned that the demand for money was narrowing political participation. Women, young people and people with valuable skills were being priced out. His comments come amid reports of widespread vote buying during the NDC’s latest internal executive elections. “It is a fact that what is happening is excluding a lot of people from the political space,” he said. “Those heavily impacted by what is happening are women and the youth because they might not have the required resources to be able to do that.” Mr Fuseini said the financial burden was also discouraging people whose integrity and reputation could benefit the country. He warned that heavy political spending creates pressure to recover the money after gaining power. “A politician is not an NGO and so when people spend that amount of money, they expect to recoup that, and that fuels corruption on a national scale.” The former NDC legislator said efforts to tackle inducement in internal elections had exposed a gap in the party’s constitution. According to him, the constitution did not clearly give the relevant party bodies authority to handle such cases. That leaves disciplinary action open to challenge. “In fact, the committee had said, our committee had said that having admitted that that thing had happened in the elections, there was a need for sanctions, but also appreciated the fact that there was no legal mechanism in our constitution to deal with that.” Fuseini said the committee was considering which institutions should handle complaints and what should count as inappropriate financial support. “How much money can we say is appropriate in the circumstances? If somebody gives a delegate GH¢200, is it an inducement or what is it?” He also raised the difficulty of dealing with payments described as transport support when the amounts exceed reasonable travel costs. The proposed framework could give constituency councils of elders authority to act or refer cases to the party’s national headquarters. Recommendations would feed into the party’s constitutional amendment process. “So yes, it’s a work in progress.”

items.title: Bam/Sabcé : Adama Siguiré appelle à l’appropriation des idéaux de la RPP
items.description: Le premier vice-président chargé du suivi des questions de développement à la Commission nationale de la Confédération des États du Sahel (AES), Adama Siguiré, a appelé samedi, à Sabcé, les populations à s’approprier les idéaux de la Révolution progressiste populaire (RPP), impulsée par le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, pour promouvoir un développement endogène fondé sur la mobilisation populaire et la cohésion sociale. Le Camarade Siguiré s’exprimait lors d’une conférence publique organisée par l’Association citoyenne pour le développement (ACD) sur le thème « Résilience et cohésion sociale pour un développement endogène : renforcer la collaboration entre la commune de Sabcé, les communautés environnantes et Bissa Gold pour une synergie collective au service du développement local, dans la dynamique de la Révolution progressiste populaire (RPP) ». Pour justifier la nécessité de repenser les priorités nationales, le conférencier a évoqué le financement des élections et celui de la lutte contre le terrorisme. « Aux dernières élections pilotées par Newton Ahmed Barry, le Burkina avait besoin de cent milliards de FCFA. Quatre-vingt-sept milliards étaient disponibles, soit quarante-sept milliards mobilisés par l’État et quarante milliards financés par les partenaires techniques et financiers. Mais pour financer notre guerre, les mêmes partenaires ne sont pas en mesure de nous donner un seul milliard », a-t-il déclaré. Selon Adama Siguiré, cette situation illustre les limites d’un modèle de gouvernance qu’il estime inadapté aux priorités du pays. Il a soutenu que la décision du Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré de mettre fin à cette forme de gouvernance vise à recentrer les efforts sur le développement national. Outre cette communication, le responsable des relations communautaires de Bissa Gold, Kayaba Kaboré, a entretenu les participants sur les grandes actions de la mine, notamment sur les nuisances comme la poussière, source de nombreuses récriminations. Représentant le directeur pays de Bissa Gold, parrain de la conférence, Léopold Bado a salué l’initiative de l’ACD. Il a réitéré la volonté de la société minière de poursuivre sa collaboration avec l’État et les communautés locales dans une dynamique de partenariat équitable et durable, au bénéfice du développement local. « Nous devons remplacer les malentendus par une concertation continue et le respect mutuel. Les autorités provinciales et communales, les représentants des communautés ainsi que les acteurs économiques ont chacun un rôle à jouer pour consolider la confiance, favoriser le dialogue et construire des partenariats au service du développement local. Je souhaite que les travaux de ce jour aillent au-delà des simples constats et permettent de formuler des propositions concrètes en faveur de la résilience, de la cohésion sociale et du développement local », a-t-il relevé. Le secrétaire général de l’ACD, Wilfried Ouédraogo, a expliqué que l’organisation de cette conférence visait à promouvoir la cohésion sociale dans la commune de Sabcé. items.title: Russell Brand told police he never had non-consensual sex
items.description: Russell Brand told police in interviews in response to allegations of rape and sexual assault that he had been “very promiscuous” in the past, but had never engaged in “non-consensual sexual activity”, a court has heard. Officers interviewed Brand four times between 2023 and 2025. The TV and media personality is currently on trial at Southwark Crown Court in London on three counts of rape and other offences. He denies all the charges. Jurors heard on Tuesday that he gave a prepared statement in each police interview. In November 2023, he said: “I have repeatedly stated publicly and written extensively that I led a very promiscuous life, that I have spent years openly denouncing. I have never engaged in non-consensual activity.” Russell Brand’s wife Laura accompanied him to court on Tuesday Brand went on to say the allegations were made in “a defamatory and fictitious documentary”, which he said contained “false and anonymised” interviews. He added that “subsequently both the media and the police publicly invited additional allegations to be made, which has resulted in further encounters to be invented or reimagined”. In court on Tuesday, the jury was also asked formally to find Brand not guilty of a charge of indecent assault. The judge, Mr Justice Bennathan, said there was “insufficient evidence to support the charge of indecent assault”. This charge related to a woman who said Brand grabbed her arm and tried to drag her into a toilet in 2001 when she worked at MTV. The jury was then given an amended indictment, which charges Brand with attempted indecent assault. Brand has pleaded not guilty to this charge. The prosecution will conclude on Wednesday morning before the defence is expected to start. Brand denies three counts of rape, three charges of sexual assault and one of attempted indecent assault.

items.title: Delay in compensation for seafarers’ families alarms Senate committee
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Senate Functio­nal Committee on Human Rights on Tuesday expressed concern over delays in compensation to families of Pakistani seafarers affected by a hostage-taking incident off Somalia. The committee, chaired by Senator Samina Mumtaz Zehri, also discussed cybercrime, crypto-currency related scams, fraudulent investment schemes and the circulation of inappropriate content targeting children on social media. Taking up the case of Pakistani seafarers, the committee sought explanations from officials over delays in the crew’s release, repatriation of a deceased seafarer’s body, medical treatment for injured crew members and financial assistance to affected families. Director of the Shipping Wing Arif Haroon briefed the committee on the incident. Members were informed that discussions were underway between the ship owner, the manning agency and parties associated with protection and indemnity insurance over compensation payments. Senator Quratul Ain Marri sought details of assistance provided by the federal government to the families of deceased seafarers. Senator Samina Mumtaz Zehri directed the authorities to submit a complete record of crew salaries, medical treatment and financial payments made from April to September. They were also asked to verify reports regarding the prime minister’s announcement of financial assistance and provide details of the amount paid to the families. The chairperson stressed that insurance-related procedures and disputes among the parties concerned should not cause unnecessary delays in payments to affected families. She sought a comprehensive report on compensation, medical facilities and assistance provided to the victims. The committee also expressed concern over the growing incidence of cybercrime, ransom-ware attacks, cryptocurrency fraud and schemes promising unusually high returns on investments. Members raised questions about delays in registering complaints and completing investigations, fraudulent calls, misuse of WhatsApp accounts and personal identification information, suspicious bank accounts and the alleged illegal use of SIM cards. The chairperson called for clear timelines for processing complaints and a mechanism to keep victims informed about progress in their cases. She also asked the relevant authorities to provide verifiable statistics on investigations, recovery of funds and legal proceedings against suspects. Officials informed the committee that suspicious accounts had been frozen in some cases, while the recovery and return of money were being processed in accordance with court orders and applicable laws. The committee also reviewed complaints involving people allegedly defrauded by companies and consultants offering overseas education, study visas and employment opportunities. The chairperson called for verification of the legal status of consultancy firms and effective action against those involved in fraud. The committee took exception to the absence of representatives of the Higher Education Commission and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, particularly as the meeting dealt with complaints involving foreign admissions and visa processes. Published in Dawn, October 28th, 2026

items.title: GoldBod’s intervention in forex market gives cedi modest reprieve; one dollar going for GH¢12.15 at forex bureaus
items.description: The intervention by GoldBod in the foreign exchange market in the last three weeks has given the cedi a modest reprieve. The Board injected a US$130 million spot foreign exchange sale at GH¢11.60 per dollar to shore up the value of the local currency By the close of the fortnight, the local currency modestly clawed back some losses in the interbank market. It appreciated 1.20% against the US dollar and pound sterling to close trading at GH¢11.65 per US dollar and GH¢15.57 per pound sterling, respectively. It also gained 0.16% against the euro to sell at GH¢13.04. In the retail market, the cedi held steady against the American greenback to trade at GH¢12.10. It appreciated by 0.32% against the pound to sell at GH¢15.85 and 1.11% against the euro to trade at GH¢13.50 to the euro. As part of its October 2026 programme, GoldBod planned to supply US$1 billion to commercial banks and provide an additional US$500 million to the Bank of Ghana for reserve accumulation. items.title: India deploys extra forces after protests against dam
items.description: GUWAHATI: India has deployed hundreds of additional security personnel in its remote northeast, authorities said on Tuesday, after youth protesters clashed with police last week over a plan to build a mega-dam to counter a Chinese hydropower project upstream. Protests in Arunachal Pradesh’s Siang Valley, which borders Tibet, turned violent last week, triggering clashes with police, who made at least 21 arrests. Police fired tear gas shells, while youth protesters pelted stones and set fire to a police station and an office of the state-owned National Hydroelectric Pow­er Corporation, authorities said. “Forces are being increased in the places where it is required. We do not want any law and order problem,” SD Singh Jamwal, police chief of Arunachal Pradesh, told Reuters. Sporadic protests have taken place in the Siang Valley in the last two years, the location of the proposed 11,200-megawatt Siang Upper Multipurpose Project, which will be developed by state-run National Hydroelectric Power Corporation. Villagers who oppose the project fear that the dam would submerge ancestral villages belonging to the Adi tribe. “We will keep opposing this dam till they cancel it. If it is constructed, 27 of our ancestral villages will be completely submerged. At least 40 or 50 more will be affected,” Gegong Jijong of the Siang Indigenous Farmers’ Forum told Reuters. The Siang river flows into Arunachal Pradesh from Tibet, where it is known as the Yarlung Zangbo. China anno­unced plans in December 2024 to build the world’s largest hydropower dam upstream, triggering fears in New Delhi that its longtime strategic rival could weaponise its control of the river. China claims Arunachal Pradesh, which it calls Zangnan, as part of southern Tibet. India says the state is an integral and inalienable part of its territory. Arunachal Pradesh’s BJP-aligned chief minister has called the Chinese project an existential threat. Published in Dawn, October 28th, 2026

items.title: Deaths in detention cells in Nigeria were entirely preventable, inquiry finds
items.description: An inquiry into the deaths of 33 detainees in Nigeria’s Minna state has found they died as a result of severe overcrowding, poor ventilation and failure by officers to respond to distress calls. Forensic and medical evidence showed the “entirely preventable” deaths had resulted from acute respiratory failure linked to prolonged confinement, aggravated by heat stress and dehydration. The evidence did not support initial claims of a disease outbreak. The detainees were found dead on 17 September while being held by the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps on suspicion of illegal mining. The investigation found that the mining sites had been licensed. Interior Minister Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo said those found responsible for the deaths would face the full force of the law. He added that investigators arrived after the detention hall had been cleaned, raising concerns about possible attempts to compromise evidence. Implicated officers will face suspension, and the report would be forwarded to the Attorney General of the Federation for further legal action, Tunji-Ojo said. The investigating committee found that the raid on the miners had been conducted without an approved operational order, proper planning or consultation with the Mining Marshals Unit. It said that 50 detainees had been held in a cell measuring about 20 sq m, with no running water or functioning toilet, and inadequate food, drinking water and airflow. Adults and minors were detained together, and some detainees were held beyond lawful detention periods. Officers reportedly ignored repeated calls for help, despite a medical worker having raised concerns about the conditions. “Detainees repeatedly banged on cell doors and walls, shouted for assistance and pleaded for water,” said the head of the investigating team, Jonathan Kure. “These distress calls were heard by officers assigned to nearby duties… but were not acted upon.” Kure said the detention conditions amounted to cruel, inhuman and degrading treatment. “The tragedy demonstrates the consequences of systemic disregard for detention standards, supervisory responsibilities and the welfare of persons in custody,” he added. The investigating committee also recommended compensation of 30m naira (£16,683; $22,285) for each of the bereaved families and 10m naira for each survivor.

items.title: Controversial Islamic cleric shot dead in northern Nigeria
items.description: A controversial Islamic cleric in Nigeria has been murdered outside his home in the northern state of Katsina. Two assailants arrived on a motorcycle and shot Yahaya Masussuka in the town of Dutsin-Ma as he was saying goodbye to visitors on Monday evening, sources told the BBC. The 47-year-old preacher and one of his guests, who was also shot, were rushed to hospital but both were pronounced dead by the attending doctor, police said. It is not clear why Masussuka was targeted, but the cleric had received death threats on social media where he posted videos in which he rejected some elements of mainstream Islam, including what happens to people after their death. It is widely believed in Islam that a person’s soul will be questioned in the grave by two angels. If they answer correctly, their soul sleeps peacefully until the Day of Judgement; if not, it is tormented. This understanding comes from what is known as the Hadith, a collection of texts believed to be the Prophet Muhammad’s spoken words and actions. This serves as a key source of Islamic knowledge for interpreting the Quran, the central religious text of Islam. But Musaylima based his teachings mainly on what was in Islam’s holy book, questioned some of the hadiths, and did not believe that the dead were reawakened. He was jailed for nine months because he teased respected scholars about their belief in this hadith and other teachings. Masussuka, who had two wives and seven children, began preaching in Quranic schools at age 13. He later attended Al-Azhar University in Egypt and later went to Oman for further studies. At home, he had a studio where he recorded videos of his teachings to broadcast on social media for his followers. The cleric was also outspoken about violent extremism, radicalisation and openly advocated for interfaith dialogue and peaceful coexistence between Muslims and Christians, who make up nearly equal parts of Nigeria’s population. Thousands of Christians and Muslims have been killed in ethnic and religious violence here over the past 25 years. For Masussuka’s efforts, Nigeria’s Network for Good Governance and Transparency honoured him with a Peace Ambassador Award last year. Six other prominent Muslim preachers have been murdered over the last two decades in northern Nigeria – several targeted by Boko Haram for criticising the jihadist group that began its insurgency in 2009. Founded in north-eastern Nigeria, it opposes Western culture, education, and the secular government, and its political goal is the creation of an Islamic state.

Que le Seigneur, dans son infinie bonté, vous bénisse abondamment et vous rende au centuple tout le bien que vous avez manifesté à son égard. « Je suis la résurrection et la vie. items.title: La Pleasure Beach management sues SSNIT, two hotels over demolition
items.description: The dispute over the management of La Pleasure Beach has taken a legal turn, with the beach’s management committee suing two hotel companies and the Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT) over the demolition of its office and other structures. In a writ of summons filed at the High Court in Accra on October 23, Stanley Anyetei Nunoo, who describes himself as Chairman of the Management Committee of La Pleasure Beach, is seeking declarations confirming the committee’s authority to manage the beachfront, regulate activities, issue licences and generate revenue from its operations. The suit accuses Hotel Investments (Ghana) Limited, La Palm Beach Hotel Limited and SSNIT of involvement in an operation that allegedly destroyed the committee’s management office and other licensed facilities, disrupting its work and affecting operators at the beach. The plaintiff describes the demolition as unlawful and is asking the court to determine whether the defendants had any legal basis for the action. Committee contests authority over beach At the centre of the case is a dispute over who has the legal authority to manage La Pleasure Beach. According to the statement of claim, the management committee was established following a Court of Appeal order dated July 21, 2022, which the plaintiff says dissolved an interim management committee set up by the High Court in April 2013. Mr Nunoo contends that the committee has since exercised management responsibilities, including issuing licences to operators, regulating activities and collecting revenue. The suit also challenges the position of the two hotel companies, which operate Labadi Beach Hotel and La Palm Beach Hotel. The plaintiff argues that the companies have no proprietary or possessory interest in La Pleasure Beach or its management, apart from an access licence granted by the committee. Demolition allegedly carried out at dawn The statement of claim alleges that security personnel from the Ghana Police Service and the Ghana Armed Forces entered the beachfront at dawn on or about October 2, 2026, and pulled down the committee’s management office and other structures. The plaintiff further claims that equipment, furniture, files, records and other property were destroyed or removed during the operation. Staff and licensed operators were allegedly driven away, disrupting the committee’s activities and the businesses operating under its authority. The suit maintains that the demolition took place without a court order or warrant and without prior notice or a hearing for the committee. Mr Nunoo is asking the court to establish the legality of the operation and determine the extent to which the defendants were involved in, or facilitated, the demolition. SSNIT’s concerns over beachfront activities The court action also refers to a press release issued by SSNIT on October 2, 2026, in which the trust said it had sought the intervention of the National Security Council Secretariat over what it described as persistent unlawful occupation, encroachment and unauthorised activities on the beachfront adjoining Labadi Beach Hotel and La Palm Royal Beach Hotel. According to the statement cited in the court documents, SSNIT said the hotels were part of its investment portfolio and that it had a responsibility to protect those investments for the benefit of contributors and pensioners. The plaintiff, however, alleges that the defendants jointly participated in or facilitated the demolition of the committee’s structures. The competing positions bring the management of the beachfront, the scope of the parties’ respective rights and the circumstances surrounding the demolition before the court for determination. The court is yet to determine the claims and reliefs sought in the action.

items.title: Vote-buying: Heavy political spending fuels corruption – Inusah Fuseini
items.description: Former NDC MP for Tamale Central, Inusah Fuseini, has warned that heavy political spending fuels corruption as politicians seek to recover the money they spend to win power. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Tuesday, he said the financial demands of politics also exclude women, young people, and people with integrity. “Also, when you spend a lot of money, politics is not Father Christmas. A politician is not an NGO, and so when people spend that amount of money, they expect to recoup that, and that fuels corruption on a national scale.” His warning comes amid reports of widespread alleged vote-buying during the NDC’s latest constituency executive elections. Mr Fuseini said the growing influence of money was narrowing access to political office. Those without substantial resources were being pushed out. “Those heavily impacted by what is happening are women and the youth because they might not have the required resources to be able to do that,” he said. He added that people with integrity and reputations for public service were shying away from politics because they could not afford its financial demands. Mr Fuseini said efforts to address inducement had exposed gaps in the NDC’s constitution. His committee recognised the need for sanctions after acknowledging that inducement had occurred during the elections. However, it found “there was no legal mechanism in our constitution to deal with that”. He explained that the party needed clear provisions defining misconduct and identifying the body authorised to handle complaints. Without those rules, disciplinary action could face challenges. “So we need a framework,” he said. The committee is considering whether constituency councils of elders should handle cases locally. Another option would be to refer offenders to the national headquarters for the Functional Executive Committee to act. It is also examining the boundary between legitimate support and inducement. “How much money can we say is appropriate in the circumstances?” he asked. “If somebody gives a delegate GH¢200, is it an inducement or what is it?” He also questioned how the party should handle payments described as transport allowances when the amounts exceed reasonable travel costs. Mr Fuseini said the party would further scrutinise the proposals before presenting them to a special congress for constitutional amendment.

items.title: Le déficit budgétaire s'allège à 33,1 MMDH à fin septembre
items.description: La situation des charges et ressources du Trésor (SCRT) fait ressortir un déficit budgétaire de 33,1 milliards de dirhams (MMDH) au terme des neuf premiers mois de 2026, contre 52,4 MMDH un an auparavant, selon ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Performance publique. Cette évolution reflète une progression des recettes ordinaires (+43,7 MMDH) supérieure à celle des dépenses (+24,5 MMDH), conjuguée à une nette amélioration du solde des comptes spéciaux du Trésor, explique le ministère dans son récent document sur la SCRT. Les recettes nettes des remboursements, dégrèvements et restitutions fiscaux, qui ont progressé de 14,8% à 338,8 MMDH, ont porté leur taux de réalisation à 78,3% des prévisions de la loi de finances (LF) de l'année 2026. Les recettes fiscales ont augmenté de 11,7%, avec un taux de réalisation de 78,7% des prévisions de la LF 2026. Cette évolution s'est accompagnée d'une hausse de près de 2,5 MMDH des remboursements, dégrèvements et restitutions fiscaux, y compris la part supportée par les collectivités territoriales (CT), dont le montant a atteint 20,7 MMDH. Quant aux recettes non fiscales, elles se sont élevées à 46,7 MMDH à fin septembre dernier, provenant notamment des produits versés par les établissements et entreprises publics (EEP) de 16,8 MMDH, dont 6,2 MMDH par l'OCP, 4,4 MMDH versés par Bank Al-Maghrib et 4 MMDH par l'Agence nationale de la conservation foncière, du cadastre et de la cartographie (ANCFCC). Elles comprennent également des recettes au titre des mécanismes de financement innovants pour un montant de 20,1 MMDH. S'agissant des dépenses ordinaires, elles se sont situées à 290,7 MMDH au terme des neuf premiers mois de cette année, affichant un taux d'exécution de 76,6% et une hausse de 9,3% par rapport à fin septembre 2025. Cette évolution résulte notamment de la hausse des dépenses au titre des biens et services de 9,6%, conjuguée à l'augmentation des intérêts de la dette de 5,9% et des charges de compensation de 13,3%. L'évolution des recettes et des dépenses ordinaires s'est traduite par une amélioration du solde ordinaire, qui a dégagé un excédent de 48,2 MMDH à fin septembre 2026, contre 29,3 MMDH un an auparavant. Par ailleurs, l'effort d’investissement public s'est poursuivi, avec des dépenses d'investissement atteignant 82,8 MMDH (+13,4%). Cette progression, supérieure à celle des dépenses globales, porte le taux de réalisation des dépenses d'investissement à 72,1%. Pour ce qui est des comptes spéciaux du Trésor (CST), ils ont dégagé un excédent de 1,5 MMDH, contre un solde débiteur de 8,7 MMDH à fin septembre 2025, soit une amélioration de 10,2 MMDH. Ce solde résulte notamment des excédents dégagés par les comptes d'affectation spéciale de 1,3 MMDH et les comptes de dépenses sur dotations de 637 millions de dirhams (MDH). La SCRT est le document statistique qui présente, au nom du ministère de l'Economie, des Finances et de la Performance publique, les résultats de l'exécution des prévisions de la loi de finances avec une comparaison par rapport aux réalisations de la même période de l'année précédente. À la différence de la situation produite par la Trésorerie Générale du Royaume (TGR), qui a un caractère fondamentalement comptable, la SCRT appréhende, comme le préconisent les normes internationales en matière de statistiques des finances publiques, les transactions économiques réalisées au cours d'une période budgétaire en décrivant, en termes de flux, les recettes ordinaires, les dépenses ordinaires, les dépenses d'investissement, le déficit budgétaire, le besoin de financement et les financements mobilisés pour la couverture de ce besoin. The post Le déficit budgétaire s'allège à 33,1 MMDH à fin septembre appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Fake drinks may be causing liver, kidney diseases in Ondo — NMA
items.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure The Ondo State chapter of the Nigerian Medical Association (NMA) has raised the alarm over the circulation of suspected fake and adulterated beverages, warning that they may be contributing to liver and kidney diseases among young people. The association recalled previous incidents involving suspected adulterated drinks in parts of the state in which at least 50 people reportedly died, and called on the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC) and other relevant agencies to intensify efforts to rid the market of counterfeit alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages. The NMA Chairman in Ondo State, Dr Roland Bola Arohunmolase, raised the concern in Akure while speaking with journalists, saying doctors were encountering liver cirrhosis and kidney disease among younger patients in age groups where such conditions were considered uncommon. He said the association could not yet provide a definitive number of cases linked to suspected adulterated drinks because investigations were ongoing, but described the changing age profile of patients as worrisome. “Traditionally, when you profile some diseases, there are certain age groups in which you do not commonly find them. When a disease no longer conforms to its traditional profile, it becomes a cause for concern,” he said. Arohunmolase said cases of liver cirrhosis among teenagers and liver and kidney diseases among people aged between 22 and 30 required closer medical investigation. “For instance, I don’t expect a child of 15 years or someone between 15 and 18 to develop liver cirrhosis. You begin to wonder why that would happen. Similarly, we are finding liver cirrhosis and kidney disease among young people between the ages of 22 and 30. I think it calls for caution,” he said. The NMA chairman identified the consumption of unhealthy or adulterated beverages as a possible risk factor, while stressing that further investigations were necessary to establish the causes of individual cases. He recalled previous incidents in Odigbo and Irele involving suspected adulterated drinks, which reportedly claimed at least 50 lives, as well as an earlier incident in Ilere linked to methanol consumption. He warned that methanol, an industrial chemical, could cause severe poisoning and organ damage when ingested. According to the association, suspected counterfeit beverages are no longer confined to open markets, as such products have allegedly found their way into supermarkets, hotels, bars and other retail outlets. It warned that beverages produced under unhygienic conditions or made with contaminated water and harmful industrial chemicals could expose consumers to acute poisoning and long-term organ damage. The association called on the FCCPC, the Ondo State Government and other relevant regulatory agencies to conduct aggressive, unannounced inspections of markets, supermarkets, hotels, bars and shops suspected of stocking counterfeit beverages. It also urged the authorities to seize and destroy products that fail to meet safety standards and prosecute those found responsible for their production and distribution. The NMA further called on beverage manufacturers to strengthen anti-counterfeiting measures through tamper-proof seals, holograms, unique QR codes and product-tracking systems to enable consumers to verify the authenticity of their purchases. It advised consumers to be wary of drinks sold at prices significantly below prevailing market rates and to inspect seals, labels and packaging before making purchases. Arohunmolase said the association decided to alert the public without delay rather than wait for bureaucratic procedures to run their course. “As medical professionals who are supposed to be the custodians of public health, we needed to bring this to the public’s notice before writing to the relevant authorities,” he said. He urged anyone who suspected they had consumed a fake or contaminated beverage to seek medical attention immediately, rather than wait for symptoms to develop. “Whenever you consume something you suspect is not okay, it may not be advisable to wait until the symptoms start manifesting. You should seek medical advice on time,” he added. The post Fake drinks may be causing liver, kidney diseases in Ondo — NMA appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Pakistan warns against escalation in Iran crisis, urges diplomacy
items.description: WASHINGTON: Pakistan has warned that the situation surrounding Iran’s nuclear programme has sharply deteriorated, urging all sides to exercise restraint and resolve the dispute through diplomacy amid continued hostilities and divisions within the UN Security Council. Speaking at a council briefing on Iran and nuclear non-proliferation on Tuesday, Pakistan’s Acting Permanent Representative, Ambassador Usman Jadoon, said mounting tensions and a lack of consensus had made a diplomatic settlement more urgent. “Pakistan remains concerned that the situation regarding the Iran nuclear file has sharply deteriorated, negatively impacting the consideration of the issue, including in the Security Council,” he said. The dispute centres on international concerns over Iran’s nuclear activities and the verification of its commitments under the non-proliferation regime. The 2015 nuclear agreement between Iran and world powers sought to limit Tehran’s nuclear programme in exchange for sanctions relief, but the United States withdrew from the accord in 2018 during Donald Trump’s first presidency. Subsequent efforts to restore the agreement failed. Mr Jadoon urged all parties to avoid rhetoric and actions that could aggravate the situation. “Pakistan urges all sides to exercise restraint, refrain from irresponsible and destabilizing rhetoric, actions, and postures that could escalate tensions and increase the risk of conflict, and choose a path that delivers peace, security and stability for all,” he said. Pakistan also called for the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) to be allowed to address technical questions relating to the nuclear dispute without political interference. “We have consistently maintained that any issues of non-compliance must be addressed through competent technical bodies like the IAEA, without politicization and consistent with the relevant parties’ rights and obligations,” Mr Jadoon said. “The IAEA must be enabled to carry out its work without any hindrance and within its technical mandate,” he added. The Pakistani envoy highlighted Islamabad’s diplomatic efforts to promote de-escalation, a ceasefire and negotiations. He cited the memorandum of understanding signed in Islamabad in June as evidence that diplomatic engagement could make progress. “The Islamabad MoU signed in June is a successful manifestation of this approach. It demonstrates that progress on the diplomatic track is possible,” he said. He acknowledged the support of Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, Egypt, China and other partners, and said Pakistan’s leadership continued working towards a peaceful settlement. “We believe that diplomacy can once again deliver results in paving the way for settling contentious issues peacefully,” Mr Jadoon said. Published in Dawn, October 28th, 2026

items.title: Alara Stool: Aramoko kingmakers seek Ooni, Oyebanji’s intervention
items.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure The Alara-in-Council and residents of Aramoko-Ekiti, Ekiti State, have appealed to the Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Enitan Ogunwusi, and Governor Biodun Oyebanji to intervene in the selection of a new traditional ruler, six months after the process was suspended. The kingmakers said the prolonged delay had left the Alara stool vacant, affecting traditional institutions, cultural activities and the observance of some festivals and rites in the community. In a statement signed by the Head of Kingmakers and Asao of Aramoko-Ekiti, High Chief Julius Oladiran Adebayo, and the Secretary and Sajowa of Aramoko-Ekiti, High Chief Kolade Oyebade, the council said its appeals to the state government had yet to receive a response. They urged the Ooni, whom they described as a custodian of Yoruba culture and tradition, to appeal to Oyebanji to permit them to reconvene and conclude the selection process. According to the kingmakers, the process began in April 2026 in accordance with the Alara of Aramoko Chieftaincy Declaration and the Ekiti State Chieftaincy Law. They said three princes were shortlisted through an Ifa divination exercise conducted by Baba Araba Elebuibon, after which voting by the 12 kingmakers ended in a tie, with six votes each. The council said a second round of voting was expected to resolve the deadlock but was not held following the postponement of the process by the Commissioner for Chieftaincy Affairs. “However, six months later, the process remains suspended after the Hon. Commissioner for Chieftaincy Affairs postponed it. Our letters to government have not received a response,” the statement said. Appealing directly to the Ooni, the kingmakers said the prolonged vacancy had created uncertainty in the community and affected the performance of some traditional rites. “The stool of Alara remains vacant. Our youths are restive. Our traditional festivals and rites cannot hold,” they said. They urged the Ooni to use his influence to persuade the governor to allow the kingmakers to reconvene and complete the selection process. The council expressed confidence that the intervention of the Ooni and the cooperation of the state government would lead to a peaceful resolution of the dispute. The kingmakers also highlighted the historical and cultural ties between Aramoko-Ekiti and Ile-Ife, describing the selection of a new Alara as important to preserving the town’s customs and traditions. They said they hoped the intervention would protect and strengthen the longstanding relationship between the two communities. The statement added that the kingmakers remained confident in the Ooni’s wisdom and the governor’s respect for law and tradition.
