items.title: Luxury cruise passengers stranded in Cambodia due to soaring fuel costs
items.description: A luxury cruise ship on a years-long voyage around the world suspended operations because of extraordinarily high fuel costs, leaving passengers stranded in Cambodia. The US-based operator of Villa Vie Odyssey said it was working with passengers on disembarkation plans and “temporary living arrangements”. It is unclear how many were on board, but the nearly 200 m (656ft) vessel can carry up to 650 passengers. It departed Belfast in October 2024 for a “continuous voyage around the world”. Global fuel prices have soared since the Iran war started earlier this year. The ship’s operator said monthly fuel costs per cabin in parts of Asia have risen from $1,800 to as much as $8,000 (£6,000). The company said it had taken “significant steps to reduce fuel consumption, including slowing the itinerary and spending more time in port”. But those measures proved insufficient to “offset the extraordinary increase in fuel costs”. “Passing the full increase on to residents is not a realistic solution,” it said. The company would spend the next 60 days on “restructuring and recapitalisation”, though “no outcome is assured”, it said. The Villa Vie Odyssey’s voyage was expected to span 3.5 years and cover nearly 150 countries, according to its website. Delays arose as the ship underwent repairs, leaving passengers stranded in Belfast for months and costing the company millions of pounds. The ship was more than 750 days into its circumnavigation before it announced the suspension of its journey on Tuesday, leaving passengers stranded in Cambodia. According to its website, the Villa Vie Odyssey has several bars and restaurants, a pool deck, and a pickleball court. Permanent residencies in its cabins range from $120,000 to $440,000. These cabins are also available for rent from $3,500 a month. Bloomberg reported that around 200 passengers were on board when they were ordered to disembark in Cambodia, citing the cruise operator’s founder.

items.title: ENDIkare Festival: Ondo monarch urges patience with Tinubu’s reforms
items.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure The Owa-Ale of Ikare-Akoko in Ondo State, Oba Adegbite Adedoyin, has appealed to Nigerians to exercise patience with the economic reforms of President Bola Tinubu, expressing confidence in the country’s future under the administration. The monarch also prayed for Tinubu’s re-election, expressing the belief that the President would secure another term in office. Oba Adedoyin spoke at the conclusion of the week-long annual Okemeji Takotabo Festival in Ikare-Akoko, where prayers were offered for peace, development and progress in the community, Ondo State and Nigeria. He said the festival remained an important part of the community’s cultural heritage, inherited from its forefathers, and provided an opportunity to seek divine intervention in the affairs of the kingdom and the country. “The Okemeji Takotabo Festival is part of the cultural heritage we inherited from our forefathers. Ikare is traditionally associated with the festival, which remains an important part of our identity and history,” he said. According to the monarch, the community visited the Okemeji hilltop during this year’s celebration to pray for Ikare-Akoko, Ondo State and Nigeria. He said prayers were also offered for Tinubu, the Ondo State governor, local government officials, ministers, political leaders and residents of the community. “We asked God to guide our leaders and grant them the wisdom to govern effectively. We also prayed for the President to secure another term, believing that he is working towards building a new Nigeria,” the monarch said. Adedoyin expressed optimism that the prayers would yield positive results, saying he expected residents to return at the next edition of the festival with testimonies of answered prayers. He further stressed that peace was essential to the development of Ikare-Akoko, adding that he had continued to encourage peaceful coexistence among residents. Also speaking, the Elemure of Emure, Oba Bankole Adeyefa, commended the Ondo State Government for supporting traditional institutions and promoting the state’s cultural heritage. Adeyefa described the festival as an important initiative for strengthening traditional institutions and preserving cultural values. He added that the celebration provided an opportunity to pray for the kingdom, Ondo State and Nigeria. Similarly, the Olona of Okeagbe Quarter, High Chief Rafiu Okunade, described the festival as historic and symbolic, commending the Owa-Ale for his contributions to community development. The Oniku of Iku Quarter, High Chief Bello Mukaila, also praised the monarch and urged residents to remain law-abiding. items.title: 2027: 2.3m electorate to vote in Zamfara
items.description: Governor Dauda Lawal and 19 other governorship candidates would scramble for 2.3 million votes in the February 2027 governorship election in Zamfara state. Governor Lawal, who is seeking reelection under the platform of the All Progressives Congress, will face 19 opposition candidates in the polls. The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) said the state registered voters have risen to 2,265,175 as of August 2026. The figure represents an increase of 313,115 voters, or 16.04 per cent, compared to the 1,952,060 registered voters recorded during the 2023 general elections in the state. The Zamfara INEC Resident Electoral Commissioner, Dr Mahmuda Isah, disclosed this during the election stakeholders’ meeting on the 2027 general elections and PVC collection on Wednesday in Gusau, Zamfara. “I would like to highlight some important electoral statistics that demonstrate both the scale of our responsibilities and the significance of public participation in the electoral process,” Isah said. “The Continuous Voter Registration exercise recorded 313,115 registrations as of August 2026, representing approximately 16.04 per cent of the 2023 registered-voter figure,” he said. He noted that the figures underscore the importance of sustained voter mobilisation, effective public enlightenment and the need to maintain an accurate, credible and inclusive Register of Voters. “Registration records will continue to undergo the necessary verification and validation processes in accordance with the law and approved procedures,” Isah said. According to him, Zamfara comprises 14 Local Government Areas, 147 Registration Areas (Electoral Wards), 3,529 Polling Units, three Senatorial Districts, seven Federal Constituencies and 24 State Assembly Constituencies. “With an average of approximately 553 registered voters per Polling Unit, based on the 2023 figure, these statistics demonstrate the considerable logistical, administrative and security responsibilities involved in conducting elections across the state,” he said. Isah said successful conduct of the 2027 general elections would require meticulous planning, efficient resource deployment, effective security coordination, continuous voter education and active cooperation of all stakeholders. He emphasised that the Permanent Voter Card (PVC) remained an essential requirement for voter accreditation and participation in elections. “The commission, therefore, attaches considerable importance to ensuring that all eligible registered voters have adequate opportunities to collect their PVCs. “Following the conclusion of the ward-level collection exercise, PVC collection will continue at INEC offices in the 14 Local Government Areas of Zamfara, in accordance with the commission’s approved arrangements. “I appeal to all registered voters who are yet to collect their PVCs to visit their respective INEC local government offices and collect their cards personally,” he said. “INEC Zamfara remains resolutely committed to carrying out its constitutional mandate with independence, impartiality, professionalism, transparency and integrity,” he assured. items.title: Zamfara steps up Ebola surveillance, screening
items.description: The Zamfara Government had stepped up surveillance against Ebola by conducting mass screening at the Gusau International Airport and across motor parks. This was done to prevent possible spread of the virus in the state. The Commissioner for Health, Dr Nafisa Maradun, disclosed this while flagging-off the response team at the Gusau International Airport on Friday. She said the state government initiated the response measure following the arrival of a passenger, an indigene of Zamfara, from Saudi Arabia via EgyptAir, who presented with high temperature. Maradun said the measures were aimed at preventing an outbreak of the virus in the state. She said the government had also intensified screening of passengers and commuters arriving at Gusau motor parks and other entry points, noting that raising public awareness remained key to curbing possible spread of the virus. The move, according to the commissioner, follows the reported index case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja. The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention had disclosed that the index patient diagnosed with the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus in Nigeria is a Ugandan-born woman who arrived in the FCT with her husband on October 3. Flagging off the response at the airport, Maradun said: “It becomes necessary as the surveillance team identified a passenger arriving from Saudi Arabia via EgyptAir with high temperature.” She said officials had been deployed to the airport to screen passengers arriving in Zamfara by air to ensure no one imports the Ebola virus into the state. items.title: ‘A politician is not an NGO’ – Inusah Fuseini on the cost of seeking office
items.description: Former NDC MP for Tamale Central, Inusah Fuseini, warned that politicians who spend heavily to win office expect to recoup their money, fuelling corruption nationwide. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Tuesday, he linked the rising cost of political contests to corruption and the exclusion of capable people from public life. “A politician is not an NGO, and so when people spend that amount of money, they expect to recoup that, and that fuels corruption on a national scale.” His warning comes amid reports of widespread alleged vote-buying during the NDC’s latest internal executive elections. The controversy has raised questions about the cost of competing and the party’s ability to punish inducement. For Mr Fuseini, the consequences reach beyond the outcome of any single contest. Financial demands are determining who can enter politics and who must stay away. “Those heavily impacted by what is happening are women and the youth because they might not have the required resources to be able to do that,” he said. He said people with integrity and reputations for service were also shying away from politics because they could not afford the sums involved. “Politics is not Father Christmas,” he said. Mr Fuseini said efforts to address inducement had exposed a gap in the NDC’s constitution. His committee recognised the need for sanctions after acknowledging that inducement had occurred during the elections. But it also found that “there was no legal mechanism in our constitution to deal with that”. He explained that the party needed rules that define the misconduct and identify the bodies authorised to handle complaints. Without those provisions, disciplinary action could face challenges. “So we need a framework.” The committee is also examining where legitimate assistance ends and inducement begins. “How much money can we say is appropriate in the circumstances?” he asked. “If somebody gives a delegate GH¢200, is it an inducement or what is it?” He questioned how the party should treat payments described as transport support when they exceed reasonable travel costs. Proposals under consideration include empowering constituency councils of elders to handle cases or referring offenders to the national headquarters. Mr Fuseini said the recommendations would undergo further scrutiny before being presented to a special congress for constitutional amendment.

items.title: Neil Young again sues Trump campaign for playing Rockin’ in the Free World at rally
items.description: Rock veteran Neil Young has filed a $10m lawsuit against a fundraising committee supporting US President Donald Trump, citing the “unauthorised” use of his 1989 song Rockin’ in the Free World. The Canadian-American star alleges that the Trump 47 Committee infringed on his copyright when it played the song before Trump took the stage at a 12 October rally in Ohio. The lawsuit says playing the song amounts to an “unauthorised public performance”. The singer-songwriter sued the Trump re-election campaign in 2020 over its use of the same song and Devil’s Sidewalk. Young said the parties settled the matter shortly thereafter. The BBC has contacted the Republican National Committee for comment. The White House referred the BBC to the Republican National Committee for comment. Through his company, Silver Fiddle Music, Young alleges the song was played without a license or Young’s permission at a political event in Youngstown, Ohio, on 12 October. In the US, music used at campaign rallies often requires a public performance licence for it to be played for an audience, even if a campaign has already purchased a legal copy of the recording. According to the US Congress, because sound recordings lack a general public-performance right, permission is needed only from the musical-work copyright holders, which can be obtained directly from them or through performing rights organisations. The five-page federal lawsuit says that Trump “was personally aware that a license would be required to play the Song at rallies,” and that Young “has not, and would not, grant the required license”. It also says the song has been played “numerous times at other rallies”. The Grammy Award winner, 80, who has strongly opposed Trump’s politics, characterises the song as “a blistering anthem that contrasts the hollow promises of American political rhetoric with the harsh realities faced by the poor, homeless and forgotten”. Young says that the song is “the opposite of everything that Donald J Trump stands for”. In 2020, Young sued Trump’s re-election campaign for copyright infringement over the same song, as well as Devil’s Sidewalk. The new lawsuit claims the campaign, at the time, “asserted no defence and immediately settled shortly after it was served”, promising never to use the song without permission again. Young posted about the lawsuit on his website on Tuesday, thanking Trump for coming to so many of his shows in the 1980s and 1990s, but stopped short of allowing him to play his music. “I am sorry it came to this, but money and transactions are something you understand,” he wrote. Young, The Rolling Stones, Rihanna, Adele, REM and the estate of Prince have previously criticised the president for using their music at campaign events.

items.title: Chinese invasion of Nigerian retail market
items.description: Nigeria must resolve the growing tension between Chinese retailers and indigenous traders without sacrificing consumers’ right of access to affordable goods. The bullish expansion of Chinese retail giant Sinomart International into Lagos, Ota, Ibadan and Enugu, with eyes on other Nigerian cities, has sharpened a dispute that erupted with protests at Lagos International Trade Fair Complex in September 2026. It also surfaced in Kano in October, with indigenous traders threatening to chase Chinese retailers out of Kano markets. Traditionally, Chinese manufacturers supplied Nigerian importers and wholesalers, who financed shipments, cleared customs, absorbed exchange-rate and logistics risks, and distributed goods to retailers. Retailers then sold to consumers. Some Chinese suppliers are moving moving downstream, selling directly to customers of Nigerian businesses. Traders say they cannot compete with suppliers buying from factories and selling near their own purchase prices. Sinomart is the best-known Chinese government-backed superstore in this expansion. Its outlets sell electronics, furniture, kitchenware, clothing, groceries, cosmetics and household goods. The dispute also involves Chinese merchants in specialist markets, including phone and auto-spare-parts trading. Available reporting does not establish that every Chinese retailer belongs to Sinomart or follows the same business model. No single recent policy created this opening. It reflects Nigeria’s investment framework, which permits foreign participation in many sectors subject to business, immigration, tax and product rules. The question is whether regulations clearly distinguish wholesale supply from retailing and are consistently enforced. The advantages are real. Direct sourcing, bulk purchasing, large-scale distribution and fewer intermediaries can lower prices and widen choice. China’s government-backed manufacturing scale, dense supplier networks and factory competition make many goods cheaper than comparable products from elsewhere. Production costs and integrated supply chains matter, alongside shipping, tariffs, exchange rates and after-sales service. Cheap must not mean unsafe or substandard. The disadvantages are serious. Indigenous traders face lost customers, squeezed margins and possible closures, threatening jobs, apprenticeships and small-business capital. If foreign suppliers dominate wholesale and retail, market power may concentrate, emasculating local distributors. Protests in Lagos and the reported expulsion of Chinese traders in Kano reflect these fears. But intimidation is unacceptable. The allegations must be investigated. Disputes must not be settled by mob action because Nigeria also has citizens doing business in China. Government should audit business permits, immigration approvals, tax compliance, customs declarations and product standards, then publish clear rules governing foreign participation in retail and wholesale trade. Restrictions must be lawful, evidence-based and nondiscriminatory. Where foreign operators may retail, enforce the same obligations and competition rules that apply to Nigerians. Nigeria should welcome investment that builds factories, trains workers, transfers technology and buys locally, while helping indigenous traders access credit, reliable power, digital tools and efficient logistics. Regulators must protect our local businesses without suppressing genuine price competition. Nigerian interests must come first. items.description: Defeated presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro has arrived in the US, hours after Brazil cancelled his passports, sources have told the BBC. The right-wing candidate left the country after its Supreme Court ordered that he surrender his passports amid an investigation into alleged money laundering. Bolsonaro has not been charged and has denied the allegations. His passports were cancelled on Tuesday after he missed a deadline to hand them over to authorities, prompting widespread speculation that he may have left Brazil. Sources told BBC Brasil and BBC Mundo that Bolsonaro met with his younger brother, Eduardo, in Florida – though his exact travel route from Brazil to the US is unclear. Neither brother could be directly reached for comment. His reported arrival in the US came hours after a senior US official confirmed the US State Department would issue visas to Bolsonaro and his family and allow them entry into the country. The BBC has contacted the White House, State Department and embassies in both the US and Brazil. On Monday, Brazil’s Supreme Court ordered Bolsonaro to hand his passports to police within 24 hours as part of its alleged money-laundering probe. At the time, Bolsonaro said he had no plans to leave the country, and insisted that he would stay in Brazil to lead the opposition to his left-wing rival, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who on Sunday won the election. After he missed the deadline, Bolsonaro’s lawyers told BBC Brasil that they were “completely in the dark” about his whereabouts. “We knew nothing about this, and we still have no information about what happened,” one lawyer said. Bolsonaro has not made any public statements since Monday afternoon local time, when he posted a video on social media. Federal officers checked border crossings to establish if Bolsonaro may have travelled to neighbouring Argentina, a police source told BBC News Brasil. However, Argentine authorities told the BBC there was no record of the senator entering their country through any border crossing. Bolsonaro was already under investigation for alleged corruption over the financing of a film about his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, who was convicted of plotting a coup and is under house arrest. A separate inquiry involves alleged links to a Brazilian lawyer accused of laundering more than $1bn through a fraud scheme. Police said earlier this month they had discovered Mr Bolsonaro had access to the bank accounts of a company owned by the lawyer. Bolsonaro denied doing business with the lawyer, and described the passport confiscation as an attempt to intimidate him. In addition to that investigation, Brazil’s Supreme Court ordered police on Tuesday to examine Flávio Bolsonaro’s electoral campaign over alleged foreign funding. The 45-year-old senator suffered a stinging defeat on Sunday when Lula beat him in a presidential run-off, a result Bolsonaro had been widely expected to win. His younger brother, Eduardo Bolsonaro, lives in Texas, but was in Miami on Sunday, where he cast his vote at a polling station and attended an election viewing event streamed to his followers. Sources have told the BBC that Flávio has already met his brother, Eduardo, in Florida, though details of his exact travel route from Brazil are unclear. It’s also unclear who travelled with him or whether Flávio Bolsonaro intends to stay and live in the US. Opinion polls put him narrowly ahead of Lula, and analysts said Bolsonaro’s first-round win on 4 October meant he was likely to win the run-off. But after an early lead in the count, the veteran incumbent overtook him, becoming the first presidential candidate to overturn a first-round loss to win in the second round. Lula won 51.79% of the vote, while Bolsonaro got 48.21%. Despite trailing by 4.4 million votes, Bolsonaro has not conceded and has called for the election to be annulled. He argues he was put at a disadvantage because polling was extended by two hours on election day, even though both his party and his rival’s requested the extension. He called the extension, which was ordered by a Supreme Court justice, a “dirty trick”. However, the party he represented, the Liberal Party, accepted the result, though it said the extension of voting “merits investigation”.

items.title: 1,500 prisoners to be shifted to Islamabad Model Jail in first phase: Naqvi
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Tuesday said prisoners from Islamabad will be shifted to the new model jail in the capital which is awaiting inauguration by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. Talking to media at the newly-built Islamabad Model Jail at H-16, Mr Naqvi, accompanied by State Minister for Interior Talal Chaudhry, said the jail project had been completed and would be inaugurated within “two to four days” by the prime minister. He said that around 1,500 Islamabad-based prisoners will be shifted to the new facility. Mr Naqvi said there were 3,300 prisoners from Islamabad in Adiala Jail and out of them 1,500 will be shifted to the new prison. He said when the second phase of the Model Jail is completed, the remaining prisoners will also be shifted here. The minister gave credit to the State Minister Talal Chaudhry and the CDA chairman and his team for the early completion of the jail project. He said that the project was launched in 2009 and construction work was started in 2016. In 2024, the project was lying abandoned with hardly up to 40 to 50pc completion. He said with the efforts of the state minister and the CDA this project has now been completed. The minister also visited various sections of the jail including the 35-bed hospital and kitchen. It is relevant to note here that the jail project faced prolonged delay. It was started by the Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) administration with the federal government’s funding. The ICT and the government had authorised the now defunct Public Works Department (PWD) for execution of the project. But work remained either stuck or continued with a slow pace. In 2024, the project was handed over to CDA for execution, which managed the completion of its first phase on a fast track basis. This phase-1 project has been completed at a cost of around Rs7 billion, including fund utilised by PWD. In 2016 with the estimated cost of the project Rs3.9 billion, its completion deadline was 2019. Meanwhile, the interior minister visited Kashmir Chowk underpass and reviewed the pace and progress of ongoing construction work. The project was launched 17 days ago. “The interior minister expressed satisfaction over the pace of construction and appreciated the progress achieved so far,” read a statement issued by the interior ministry. The minister said if construction continued at the current pace, the project could be completed in less than 30 days. CDA officials said work continued at the site with full pace and it could be completed before November 5. They said after 18 days, the physical progress of the work was around 75pc. The prime minister had laid the foundation stone of this project worth Rs1.4 billion on October 6. Published in Dawn, October 28th, 2026

items.title: Judge recuses himself from bail plea of suspect in Azeri woman case
items.description: LAHORE: Additional District & Sessions Judge (AD&SJ) Rafaqat Ali Gondal on Tuesday recused himself from hearing the bail application of Ahmed Tanveer, a key suspect, in the rape case of an Azeri woman, and referred the matter to the Lahore High Court for further proceedings. Earlier, Advocate Safdar Shaheen Pirzada, counsel for the suspect, filed an application seeking exemption for his client from personal appearance before the court. The counsel stated that the suspect’s interim bail expired on Oct 27, but he could not appear before the court because he had been arrested in another case. He said Ahmed was in jail for a 14-day identification parade in connection with the other case. He asked the court to exempt the petitioner/suspect from appearing for one hearing. However, AD&SJ Gondal expressed his inability to hear the matter. The judge informed the counsel that he had prepared a reference of the matter and forwarded it to the high court for further action. Without naming a case, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, last week, had alleged that in a recent rape case, it was revealed that the suspect’s wealthy family allegedly offered huge money to the victim in exchange for withdrawing her allegations, despite her statement already having been recorded under Section 164. “It was further alleged that the judge who granted bail to the accused had also been bribed,” she added. Defence-C police had registered the case on the complaint of the Azeri woman, who accused three men of subjecting her to gang rape. She also accused two women of abetment in the crime. Now all five male and female suspects are in police custody. Published in Dawn, October 28th, 2026

items.title: One killed, five injured by Afghan firing near Angoor Adda
items.description: LOWER SOUTH WA­­Z­IRISTAN: In yet another violation of border protocols, Afghan security forces opened unprovoked fire on Pakistan Army border posts and residential areas in the Angoor Adda border area on Tuesday. The unprovoked attacks took the life of one local, while five of a family were injured when a mortar landed on their home. The unprovoked firing prompted a swift response from security forces. According to officials, the firing originated from posts located inside Afghan territory, and targeted Pakistani border posts with sniper, small and heavy weapons. Sources said that Pakistani forces launched an immediate and effective retaliatory action, engaging multiple Afghan Taliban border posts, mortar positions and defensive bunkers with small and heavy arms, including artillery. The “intense and accurate response” forced the Afghan Taliban to abandon their posts and flee. Sources reiterated that Pakistani forces have complete control over the border area. The border at Angoor Adda is one of the most important and sensitive crossings along the Pak-Afghan border, serving as a key trade route and one of the main points of public movement between the two countries. Violations from the Afghan side have become a routine matter. Afghan forces often resort to unprovoked firing without any reason, creating fear among the local tribal population and disrupting trade and daily life. Published in Dawn, October 28th, 2026

items.title: Pod of bottlenose dolphins spotted off Gwadar
items.description: GWADAR: A massive pod of more than 500 dolphins was spotted near a fishing boat in the coastal waters off Gwadar. Marine experts and environmentalists have described the sighting of such a large group of dolphins as a positive indicator of abundant marine life, rich food sources and a healthy ocean ecosystem in the region. Experts said the dolphins have been scientifically identified as Tursiops aduncus, commonly known as Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphins. Pakistan’s coastal waters, particularly along the Balochistan coast, are home to diverse marine life, including around 26 recorded species of cetaceans, such as dolphins, whales and porpoises. Highlighting the ecological significance of the sighting, marine conservationists urged authorities and local fishing communities to strengthen conservation efforts. They stressed that protecting dolphins, whales, sea turtles and other marine species is essential to maintaining the delicate balance of the coastal ecosystem. Our Staff Reporter adds from Karachi: Amir Dad Khan, who was captaining a fishing boat, spotted a remarkable group of more than 500 of these dolphins leaping near his vessel in Gwadar, according to experts associated with the World Wide Fund for Nature Pakistan (WWF-P). “The sighting of such a large pod engaging in playful activities in the shallow waters is a promising sign of a robust coastal ecosystem along Baloch­istan’s shores — and especially in Gwadar,” said Muhamad Moazzam Khan, WWF-P’s technical adviser. He added that it’s an encouraging indicator of biodiversity and a heal-thy food chain in both coastal and offshore waters. Published in Dawn, October 28th, 2026

items.title: PTI asked to look inward; warned against further talks
items.description: ISLAMABAD: A majority of PTI lawmakers on Tuesday opposed further efforts to negotiate with the powers that be, arguing that the latter had already secured what they wanted, and that pursuing further talks would “only show weakness”. Several members also expressed dissatisfaction with the party leadership’s handling of the prevailing challenges, questioning its decisions and overreliance on then-Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister Sohail Afridi. Heated arguments were witnessed during a joint parliamentary party meeting that lasted over seven hours, with some questioning why the top leadership had handed so much authority to Mr Afridi, who, they said, held no position within the party hierarchy. On the other hand, around 15 lawmakers favoured supporting the proposed 28th Amend­ment, arguing that it could help normalise relations with the establishment and pave the way for the release of Imran Khan. The meeting, held at Parl­i­ament House to discuss the prevailing political situation and the party’s future strategy, was chaired by PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan. Former National Assembly speaker Asad Qaiser, Senator Ali Zafar and Chief Whip Malik Amir Dogar were in attendance. An insider, requesting anonymity, said that most participants, including Mr Qaiser, had rejected further efforts to negotiate. Some criticised Barrister Gohar and Secretary General Salman Akram Raja, questioning why the party leadership appeared to be functioning under Mr Afridi. They alleged that the top leadership had left everything to the KP chief minister, who had become non-functional after the imposition of governor’s rule in KP, because of its interest in transfers, postings and financial matters in the province. Public support The insider said members believed that although morale had declined following the PTI government’s removal in KP, the party had not lost public support. Another participant said Mr Qaiser presented a pre-written declaration containing points that had not been discussed at the meeting, annoying several members. At this, Faisal Amin Gandapur reacted by asking, “Is this a joke?” and walked out following an exchange with Barrister Gohar. Mobeen Arif Jutt questioned why the party was not speaking up for leaders who were in jail or in hiding, saying he felt embarrassed when speaking to them. He also criticised opposition leader Mahmood Khan Achakzai, alleging that Mr Achakzai had contacted Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz after his son was arrested near Kharian and stayed in Lahore until his son was released. Azam Swati urged Barrister Gohar and his colleagues to step down, while MNA Shah Ahad also criticised the leadership. Peshawar MNA Sher Ali said party leaders were receiving calls asking them to surrender to the police or face police raids on their homes. Consultations go on After the meeting, party whip Amir Dogar said several prevailing issues had been discussed, but decisions would be taken after consultation with leaders of the opposition in both houses. This was the first session and another meeting would follow, he said. Senator Ali Zafar said the meeting had discussed possible future decisions and that committees, to be headed by the opposition leaders, would be formed. Media reports suggested that some lawmakers, including Ali Muhammad Khan, walked out of the meeting before it concluded. Published in Dawn, October 28th, 2026

items.title: GPAA opens 23rd Annual Conference in Techiman with strong calls for primary healthcare action
items.description: The Ghana Physician Assistants Association (GPAA) has officially opened its 23rd Annual General Conference at the Jemima Grace Kodua Hotel in Techiman, with a resounding call for physician assistants to be positioned at the heart of Ghana’s primary healthcare delivery system. The high-level opening ceremony brought together key stakeholders in the health sector, including the Director General of the Ghana Health Service, Dr. Samuel Kaba Akoriya; the National President of the GPAA, Peter Akudugu Ayamba; the Bono East Regional Minister’s representative, Mrs. Beatrice Kwarteng; and Nananom of the Techiman Traditional Council. “Not Background Noise” — GPAA President Delivers Stirring Message In his address, GPAA National President Peter Akudugu Ayamba delivered a powerful message on the indispensable role of physician assistants in Ghana’s healthcare architecture. “Primary healthcare is not a footnote. It is the headline. And the Physician Assistant is not background noise. They are a frontline instrument of policy delivery,” Ayamba declared. He emphasized that if the nation is serious about moving from policy to practice, there must be a deliberate effort to remove the obstacles that stand between policy formulation and community outreach. “We have to be serious about equipping physician assistants to respond fully to the rate of health needs in the community,” he added. Government Reaffirms Commitment In a speech read on behalf of the Bono East Regional Minister, Francis Owusu, the Regional Planning Officer, Mrs. Beatrice Kwarteng, reiterated the government’s commitment to supporting the work of physician assistants. “Government remains committed to supporting the works of physician assistants by providing more health facilities in rural communities to help in the implementation of the free primary healthcare policy,” Mrs. Kwarteng stated on behalf of the Regional Minister. She further noted that the government recognizes the critical role physician assistants play in bridging the healthcare gap, particularly in underserved rural communities, and assured that efforts are underway to strengthen the system. GHS Director General Charges Practitioners The Director General of the Ghana Health Service, Dr. Samuel Kaba Akoriya, also addressed the gathering, urging physician assistants to remain steadfast in their dedication to the free primary healthcare system. “Remain committed to the free primary healthcare system in order to leave positive names for yourselves,” Dr. Akoriya charged the practitioners. Traditional Council Backs Conference The traditional authority was well-represented at the ceremony. Nana Boakye Ameyaw Pentenpre II, Nifahene of the Techiman Traditional Council, who chaired the occasion on behalf of the Omanhene, urged the physician assistants to make the conference a turning point. “Let this conference be a defining moment for transformative leadership, effective policy execution, and a lasting legacy of healthcare excellence,” he said. The 23rd Annual General Conference, themed “From Policy to Practice: Positioning the Physician Assistant to Deliver Comprehensive Free Primary Healthcare at the Community Level,” is not just a talk shop. Alongside the conference activities, the GPAA has been running a free community health screening across four locations in Techiman — the forecourt of the Bonokyempem Hall, the Regional Coordinating Council (RCC), the Techiman Central Market, and the forecourt of the NHIS office. The screening, which includes breast cancer examinations and general health assessments, targets busy workers who find it difficult to visit hospitals due to their schedules. It is a practical demonstration of the conference theme in action.

items.title: Azzedine Ounahi : une opération chirurgicale envisagée, un retour repoussé à mars 2027
items.description: Azzedine Ounahi pourrait être éloigné des terrains pendant plusieurs mois. De nouveaux examens médicaux ont révélé une rupture complète du tendon du biceps fémoral de la jambe droite, poussant les médecins à privilégier une intervention chirurgicale. Son retour avec le Panathinaïkos pourrait intervenir lors des play-offs du championnat grec, en mars prochain, selon la presse locale. Le coup dur se confirme pour Azzedine Ounahi. Le milieu de terrain marocain du Panathinaïkos souffre d’une rupture complète du tendon du biceps fémoral de la jambe droite, selon de nouveaux examens médicaux rapportés par plusieurs médias grecs. La gravité de la blessure devrait conduire le joueur à subir une intervention chirurgicale, prévue jeudi prochain. L’international marocain s’était blessé le dimanche 18 octobre, lors de la rencontre de championnat face à l’Asteras Tripolis, remportée par son équipe sur le score de 5-1. Contraint de quitter la pelouse sur une civière dès la 19e minute, il avait suscité de vives inquiétudes quant à la nature de sa blessure. Les premiers espoirs d’un rétablissement moins compliqué ont été douchés par les résultats d’une seconde IRM. Celle-ci a confirmé une rupture complète du tendon, une blessure plus sérieuse que ce qui était initialement envisagé. Face à ce diagnostic, une opération a été retenue afin de limiter le risque de rechute et de permettre au joueur d’aborder sa rééducation dans les meilleures conditions possibles. Les étapes suivantes dépendront de l’évolution de son état de santé, de sa réponse au traitement et de sa progression durant la rééducation. À ce stade, aucune date définitive de reprise n’a été confirmée. Selon les informations relayées par la presse grecque, Azzedine Ounahi pourrait retrouver la compétition lors des play-offs du championnat grec, en mars 2027. Cette échéance reste toutefois indicative et dépendra du déroulement de sa convalescence. Pour le Panathinaïkos, cette indisponibilité représente un coup d’arrêt alors que le club devra composer sans l’un de ses milieux de terrain. Le joueur marocain devra désormais se concentrer sur l’opération et la rééducation, avec pour objectif de retrouver progressivement ses capacités physiques avant d’envisager un retour à la compétition. The post Azzedine Ounahi : une opération chirurgicale envisagée, un retour repoussé à mars 2027 appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Former Miss Switzerland accuses Donald Trump of rape
items.description: Donald Trump has been accused of rape by a model and former Miss Switzerland in a report produced by the Democratic Party. Beatrice Keul, who shortly before the 2024 election claimed the president had groped her in November 1993, has now alleged that Mr Trump also raped her during that incident. The report, released Monday, detailed an investigation by US House Democrats into Mr Trump’s alleged connections to Jeffrey Epstein’s crimes. The White House denied the report’s allegations, with a spokesman describing the claims as “a desperate attempt by crazed Democrats to distract Americans from the surging Republican momentum driven by President Trump ’s historic achievements”. Beatrice Keul’s account is detailed in a House Democrats’ report examining the president’s alleged ties to Jeffrey Epstein During interviews with Democratic committee staffers “over several weeks”, Ms Keul said she met Mr Trump when she was 24 at a press event for a pageant at New York’s Plaza Hotel, which he owned at the time. According to Ms Keul, Mr Trump allegedly promised that he would arrange a visa for her and said he could ensure that she got accepted into New York University (NYU). “I will take care of you,” he told her, according to the claims in the report. After Mr Trump stepped away from their conversation, Ms Keul said she was immediately approached by Epstein, who described himself as “Don’s best friend” and invited her to a party at Mar-a-Lago. “We organise many parties with Don,” Epstein apparently told her. Mr Trump says that he ended his friendship with Epstein long before there were suspicions of any criminal wrongdoing and has repeatedly described him as a “creep” whom he kicked out of his Mar-a-Lago club. According to Ms Keul, Epstein introduced himself as ‘Don’s best friend’ Credit: Getty Images/Davidoff Studios Photography According to the Democrats’ report, a representative for Mr Trump later allegedly invited Ms Keul to meet the future president upstairs at the Plaza Hotel. “Upon entering, Trump reportedly grabbed Keul from behind and forcibly raped her; in the process, tearing her dress and causing bleeding and bruising on multiple parts of her body,” the report claimed. “Keul described the rape as ‘brutal,’” the report added. Following the alleged assault, Ms Keul claimed that Mr Trump “sat her on the edge of the bed, repeated his promises to arrange for a visa and NYU admission, and made her promise she would keep quiet, saying, ‘[T]he show must go on.’” In Ms Keul’s original claims in October 2024, she accused Mr Trump of groping her at the Plaza Hotel in 1993. “He kissed me on the lips and on the neck. He tried to lift my dress. He was grabbing and touching my body everywhere he could,” she told The Daily Mail. But she said things did not go further. “I tried everything I could. Finally, I said ‘let’s talk first’ or something like that, then he slowed down,” she said. The 6ft 1in ex-model suggested it was her size that “saved her” from the alleged attack from escalating. The newspaper also reported that a longtime friend said Ms Keul “first told him her story of Trump’s unwanted sexual advances 20 years ago, and that her telling of the incident has not changed in the intervening years.” Allegations dismissed as ‘fake’ At the time, Karoline Leavitt, then press secretary to Mr Trump, described the allegations as “fake”. A White House spokesman said Mr Trump had been “fully exonerated of anything related to Epstein.” “This ‘report’ is nothing more than a desperate attempt by crazed Democrats to distract Americans from the surging Republican momentum driven by President Trump’s historic achievements,” they said. The newly released report summarises the accounts of four other women who have accused Mr Trump of rape or sexual assault. It also claims that Mr Trump, Epstein and others used the pageant at the Plaza Hotel as a “‘hunting ground’ to prey on vulnerable young women and girls.” “Five women have directly accused Trump of rape or sexual assault in Epstein’s company or presence; others have indicated that Epstein or Maxwell attempted to traffic them to Trump,” Jamie Raskin, the committee’s ranking member, said in a statement alongside the release of the report. “Trump’s Justice Department appears to be covering up these crimes to protect the President,” he added. The report landed just a week before the US midterm elections . Mr Trump’s handling of the Epstein files – along with inflation and rising energy prices caused by his war with Iran – has hamstrung Republican candidates even though the US president is not on the ballot.

items.title: Affaire des coffres-forts vidés à AFG Bank Guinée : le Tribunal de commerce condamne la banque à payer 3,7 millions de dollars à Aladji Sidibé
items.description: Screenshot " data-large-file="https://i0.wp.com/mediaguinee.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/IMG_0807.jpeg?fit=1024%2C934&ssl=1" class="wp-image-329215 size-full" src="https://i0.wp.com/mediaguinee.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/IMG_0807.jpeg?resize=1170%2C1067&ssl=1" alt="" width="1170" height="1067" srcset="https://i0.wp.com/mediaguinee.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/IMG_0807.jpeg?w=1267&ssl=1 1267w, https://i0.wp.com/mediaguinee.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/IMG_0807.jpeg?resize=300%2C274&ssl=1 300w, https://i0.wp.com/mediaguinee.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/IMG_0807.jpeg?resize=1024%2C934&ssl=1 1024w, https://i0.wp.com/mediaguinee.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/IMG_0807.jpeg?resize=768%2C701&ssl=1 768w" sizes="(max-width: 1170px) 100vw, 1170px" /> L’homme d’affaires guinéen Aladji Sidibé ‘’Wassaba’’ C’est une affaire aux lourdes implications judiciaires qui secoue la place financière de Conakry. Saisi d’un litige opposant l’opérateur économique Aladji Sidibé, dit « Wassaba », à AFG Bank Guinée SA (ancienne SGG SA), le Tribunal de commerce de Conakry a rendu sa décision le 19 octobre dernier. Retenant la responsabilité civile de l’institution bancaire dans la disparition de fonds placés sous sa garde, les juges ont condamné la banque à verser au plaignant un total de 3,7 millions de dollars, comprenant le principal et les dommages-intérêts. Chronique d’un dépôt de 6 millions de dollars L’affaire remonte au 5 février 2025. À cette date, selon le document consulté par Mediaguinée, l’opérateur économique Aladji Sidibé dépose une somme de 6 000 000 de dollars américains auprès de l’établissement bancaire. Le versement est attesté par un document signé conjointement par le client et Mamadou Yaya Diallo, alors présenté comme « Responsable de la Caisse Centrale » de la banque. Désireux d’assurer la conservation sécurisée de ses liquidités, M. Sidibé signe, dès le lendemain, un contrat de location de deux compartiments de coffres-forts portant les numéros 23 et 24. Au fil des semaines, l’opérateur effectue plusieurs retraits, selon des modalités impliquant le contrôle et l’intervention technique de la banque. L’accès à ces coffres étant soumis à une procédure réglementée, la disparition des fonds soulève des interrogations sur les conditions dans lesquelles les opérations ont été effectuées. La découverte de coffres vides et les reproches adressés à la banque La situation bascule en juin 2026. De retour du pèlerinage à La Mecque, qu’il vient d’accomplir, Aladji Sidibé souhaite effectuer un nouveau retrait sur un solde qu’il estime alors à 3 400 000 dollars. Il constate avec stupéfaction que les deux coffres sont vides. Comment des fonds confiés à la banque ont-ils pu disparaître alors que l’accès aux coffres était soumis à des procédures de contrôle ? Selon le document consulté par Mediaguinée, l’opérateur reproche à la direction de la banque de ne pas avoir diligenté les investigations nécessaires, notamment par la consultation des images de vidéosurveillance, ni pris de sanctions contre ses employés. Face à cette situation, il fait dresser un constat d’huissier, adresse une sommation à l’établissement, puis saisit la justice. Les arguments de conformité et les documents de retrait contestés Pour sa défense, AFG Bank Guinée SA a notamment évoqué un placement initial dans une « cantine », dans l’attente de justificatifs sur l’origine des fonds. La banque a également produit des pièces de retrait portant les noms de Mamadou Yaya Diallo et de Thierno Oumar Sow, censées établir que le reliquat aurait été ramené à 2 100 000 dollars, puis à 2 000 000 de dollars. Ces arguments n’ont pas convaincu le tribunal. Sur la conformité bancaire, les juges ont estimé qu’une banque qui doute de l’origine des fonds déposés par un client doit empêcher l’opération ou geler les sommes concernées dans l’attente d’éclaircissements. Elle ne peut, selon les termes rapportés dans le document, invoquer les règles de conformité pour justifier la perte de l’argent. Le tribunal a également relevé des irrégularités dans les documents produits pour justifier les retraits, notamment l’absence de signature du client. La décision indique : « Il est clair que dans la pratique bancaire, jamais deux opérations distinctes (en l’espèce des retraits) ne font l’objet du même document […] l’irrégularité est manifeste et la mention en marge, d’ailleurs non signée par Aladji Sidibé ne peut lui être opposable. » 3,7 millions de dollars de condamnation Au terme des débats, le Tribunal de commerce de Conakry, présidé par Sékou Kandé, a statué publiquement et contradictoirement. Dans sa décision, la juridiction : Retient la responsabilité civile de la banque, déclarée responsable de la disparition des fonds placés dans les coffres sous sa garde ; Condamne AFG Bank Guinée SA à verser 3 400 000 dollars à Aladji Sidibé au titre du principal ; Accorde 300 000 dollars de dommages-intérêts, portant le montant total de la condamnation à 3,7 millions de dollars ; Met les entiers dépens à la charge de la banque. Le tribunal a toutefois décidé qu’il n’y avait pas lieu à exécution provisoire de sa décision. Les modalités d’exécution du jugement restent donc susceptibles d’être affectées par un éventuel appel, selon les règles applicables. Aux dernières nouvelles, la partie défenderesse, AFG Bank Guinée SA, a relevé appel de la décision du Tribunal de commerce de Conakry. Cette affaire soulève des questions importantes sur la sécurité des fonds confiés aux établissements bancaires, la traçabilité des opérations et la responsabilité des banques envers leur clientèle. items.title: Israël : recul du camp de Netanyahu, les partis arabes en hausse selon les sondages de sortie des urnes
items.description: Les sondages de sortie des urnes publiés mardi soir en Israël placent le camp de l’opposition devant la coalition de Benjamin Netanyahu, sans qu’aucun des deux blocs n’atteigne la majorité nécessaire pour former un gouvernement. Les partis arabes réaliseraient une progression notable, avec 17 à 18 sièges estimés sur les 120 que compte la Knesset. Les premières estimations des élections législatives israéliennes dessinent un Parlement sans majorité claire. Selon les sondages de sortie des urnes diffusés par les chaînes israéliennes 12 et 13, le camp de l’opposition, conduit par Gadi Eizenkot, obtiendrait entre 52 et 53 sièges, contre 50 pour le bloc de Benjamin Netanyahu. Les deux listes arabes totaliseraient, quant à elles, entre 17 et 18 sièges. Ces projections laissent présager des négociations difficiles, alors qu’une majorité de 61 députés sur 120 est nécessaire pour former un gouvernement. Malgré l’avance globale attribuée à l’opposition, le Likoud de Benjamin Netanyahu conserverait sa position de première formation politique. La chaîne 12 lui attribue environ 24 sièges, contre 22 pour le parti Yashar de Gadi Eizenkot. Selon la chaîne 13, le Likoud obtiendrait 25 sièges et Yashar 23. D’autres formations pourraient jouer un rôle dans les négociations. Le parti BeYachad, dirigé par l’ancien Premier ministre Naftali Bennett, recueillerait entre 12 et 14 sièges. Les Démocrates de Yaïr Golan obtiendraient neuf sièges, tandis que la formation Israël Beytenou d’Avigdor Lieberman en décrocherait entre sept et neuf. À la suite de ces premières projections, plusieurs responsables de l’opposition ont estimé que les électeurs avaient exprimé leur défiance envers le gouvernement sortant. Gadi Eizenkot a notamment évoqué une perte de confiance envers Benjamin Netanyahu et son équipe, tout en affirmant sa volonté de travailler à la formation d’un nouveau gouvernement si les résultats se confirmaient. Les partis arabes renforcent leur représentation L’autre enseignement de ces estimations concerne la progression des partis arabes. Les deux listes réuniraient entre 17 et 18 sièges, contre dix lors des élections de 2022. Selon les projections de la chaîne 12, la Liste commune obtiendrait 11 sièges et la Liste arabe unie, Ra’am, sept. La chaîne 13 leur attribue ensemble 17 sièges. Cette progression pourrait leur donner davantage de poids dans les discussions parlementaires. Toutefois, aucun des deux grands blocs n’a annoncé clairement son intention de les intégrer à une éventuelle coalition gouvernementale. Leur influence dépendra donc des alliances qui pourront être nouées après la publication des résultats définitifs. Youssef Jabareen, chef de la Liste arabe unie, a déclaré que les partis arabes étaient devenus une force politique qu’il n’était plus possible d’ignorer. Il a également indiqué que les décisions à venir seraient prises de manière responsable, quelles que soient les circonstances politiques. Une participation électorale élevée Ces élections, les premières depuis l’attaque du Hamas du 7 octobre 2023, ont été marquées par une participation importante. Selon la Commission électorale centrale israélienne, le taux de participation atteignait 74,3 % à 20 heures, heure locale, soit le niveau le plus élevé enregistré à cette heure depuis 1988. Lors des élections de novembre 2022, il s’élevait à 66,3 % au même moment. Les bureaux de vote des localités arabes et de Jérusalem-Est ont notamment enregistré une forte mobilisation. Dans la ville d’Oum al-Fahm, une électrice de 23 ans interrogée par l’agence citée dans l’article a exprimé son souhait de ne plus être traitée comme une citoyenne de deuxième ou de troisième catégorie et de pouvoir vivre en paix. La campagne a également été marquée par des accusations de Benjamin Netanyahu concernant de possibles irrégularités. La Commission électorale a toutefois présenté l’affaire évoquée comme une tentative isolée de corruption d’électeurs. Le chef de Ra’am, Mansour Abbas, a rejeté les accusations du Premier ministre, les qualifiant de mensonges et d’incitation à la polémique. La formation du prochain gouvernement reste incertaine Les résultats publiés mardi soir restent provisoires. Le dépouillement doit notamment intégrer plus de 650 000 bulletins spéciaux, comprenant les votes de militaires, de diplomates, de patients et d’électeurs ayant voté hors de leur bureau habituel. Ces bulletins pourraient modifier la répartition des sièges, notamment pour les partis proches du seuil électoral de 3,25 %. Une fois les résultats définitifs annoncés, le président israélien Isaac Herzog devra consulter les partis représentés à la Knesset avant de charger un député de former un gouvernement. En attendant, les estimations ne permettent pas de déterminer quelle coalition pourra réunir les 61 sièges nécessaires. La progression des partis arabes et l’absence de majorité nette des deux principaux blocs devraient placer les négociations politiques au centre des prochains jours. The post Israël : recul du camp de Netanyahu, les partis arabes en hausse selon les sondages de sortie des urnes appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Miss Univers 2026 : Justine Kamara en route pour Porto Rico, avec l’ambition de faire briller les couleurs de la Guinée
items.description: À l’approche de la 75ᵉ édition du concours Miss Univers, prévue le 24 novembre 2026 à Porto Rico, Ela Consulting, en collaboration avec Miss Univers Guinée, a organisé un cocktail de départ en l’honneur de Justine Kamara, ce mardi 28 octobre, à Conakry. Présidée par le ministre de la Culture, du Tourisme et de l’Artisanat, Moussa Moïse Sylla, la cérémonie a été marquée par des appels à la mobilisation nationale, des témoignages de soutien et un vibrant hommage à la culture guinéenne. Prenant la parole, la présidente du comité Miss Univers Guinée, Aminata Diallo, a exprimé sa fierté d’accompagner celle qui portera les couleurs nationales à ce rendez-vous international. « Cette soirée est un moment de partage, mais aussi l’occasion de réaffirmer notre confiance à celle qui portera nos couleurs sur l’une des plus grandes scènes internationales », a-t-elle déclaré. Selon elle, le choix de Justine Kamara repose sur son expérience, son ambition, son parcours entrepreneurial et sa participation antérieure à Miss France. Au-delà de son apparence physique, la candidate présente, à ses yeux, les qualités nécessaires pour relever les défis d’une compétition internationale exigeante. « Aujourd’hui, une nouvelle étape s’ouvre à vous. Vous ne représenterez pas uniquement un concours, mais toute une nation, sa culture, ses valeurs et son potentiel », a souligné Aminata Diallo, invitant la candidate à faire preuve d’élégance, de discipline et d’assurance. Un concours pour promouvoir l’image de la Guinée Pour la présidente du comité, la participation de Justine Kamara s’inscrit dans une dynamique de présence accrue de la Guinée aux compétitions internationales. Elle a rappelé les participations de Saraba en 2024 et de Matiti Guindo Berté en 2025, avant de présenter la nouvelle candidate comme celle qui doit poursuivre cette ambition. « Notre objectif ne se limite pas à participer. Nous voulons faire honorer la Guinée, marquer les esprits et donner à notre représentante toutes les chances de se distinguer », a-t-elle affirmé. Elle a également insisté sur la dimension promotionnelle du concours, estimant que Miss Univers constitue une vitrine permettant de mettre en valeur les identités, les talents et le potentiel du pays. Elle a notamment évoqué la possibilité de contribuer au rayonnement de la Guinée en mettant en lumière ses ambitions de développement, dont le programme Simandou 2040. Dans cette perspective, elle a appelé les Guinéens de l’intérieur et de la diaspora à soutenir activement Justine Kamara, notamment en suivant ses actualités, en partageant ses publications et en participant aux votes organisés dans le cadre de la compétition. La présidente du comité a par ailleurs exprimé sa reconnaissance au président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, à la Première dame, Laurianne Doumbouya, ainsi qu’aux responsables institutionnels et aux partenaires qui accompagnent cette initiative. Elle a notamment cité le Fonds de développement des arts et de la culture (FODAC), la Fondation KPC pour l’humanitaire, la Fondation Solidarité de la Première dame, Mona Technologie et la Loterie nationale de Guinée. Justine Kamara veut porter un message en faveur des femmes et des enfants Visiblement émue par la mobilisation autour de sa candidature, Justine Kamara a exprimé sa gratitude envers les personnalités présentes, les institutions, ses partenaires et le peuple de Guinée. « Représenter la Guinée, ce n’est pas seulement porter une écharpe. C’est porter une histoire, une culture, des valeurs et l’espoir de tout un peuple », a-t-elle déclaré. Pour la candidate, cette participation dépasse largement le cadre d’un concours de beauté. Elle constitue une occasion de faire découvrir les traditions guinéennes, les paysages du pays et le potentiel de ses femmes. Dix ans après une première expérience dans l’univers des concours de beauté, Justine Kamara affirme aborder cette nouvelle étape avec davantage de maturité. Devenue entrepreneure, épouse et mère de jumelles, elle entend faire de son parcours un message d’encouragement à l’endroit des jeunes filles. « Je suis convaincue qu’une femme peut être mère, entrepreneure et engagée, tout en poursuivant ses ambitions et en croyant en ses capacités », a-t-elle expliqué. Au-delà de la compétition, la candidate entend défendre une cause qui lui tient particulièrement à cœur : la protection, la dignité et l’autonomisation des femmes et des enfants vulnérables en Guinée. À travers sa fondation S’aboni Action, elle affirme s’engager auprès de ces catégories dans les moments difficiles de leur vie. Elle souhaite notamment porter ce message sur la scène internationale à travers une vidéo intitulée « Change your life, change a generation », que l’on peut traduire par « Changez votre vie, transformez une génération ». « Lorsqu’on donne à une femme les moyens de se protéger, de s’éduquer, de devenir indépendante et de construire son avenir, c’est toute une génération que l’on transforme », a-t-elle soutenu. Consciente du niveau de la compétition, qui réunit des candidates venues de nombreux pays, Justine Kamara a néanmoins affiché sa détermination à défendre les couleurs nationales. « La Guinée a toute sa place sur les plus grandes scènes internationales, et je compte bien lui faire honneur », a-t-elle assuré, avant d’inviter ses compatriotes à s’approprier cette aventure. « Cette aventure, je ne veux pas qu’elle soit seulement la mienne. Je veux qu’elle soit la nôtre », a-t-elle lancé. La candidate a également remercié les partenaires qui contribuent à sa préparation, Elle a réservé une mention particulière à Georgette Griffiths pour son accompagnement. Georgette Griffiths appelle à soutenir la candidate guinéenne Co-organisatrice de l’événement et responsable de la structure ELA Consulting, Georgette Griffiths a, pour sa part, salué la participation de Justine Kamara et l’a encouragée à représenter dignement la Guinée à ce rendez-vous international. Elle a notamment insisté sur l’importance du soutien populaire dont la candidate aura besoin tout au long de la compétition, en lui rappelant qu’elle porte les espoirs de millions de compatriotes. Cette mobilisation, selon les organisateurs, constitue un levier essentiel pour accroître la visibilité de la candidate et renforcer la présence guinéenne dans cette compétition mondiale. Moussa Moïse Sylla célèbre la culture guinéenne dans un discours poétique Moment fort de la cérémonie, l’intervention du ministre de la Culture, du Tourisme et de l’Artisanat, Moussa Moïse Sylla, a pris la forme d’un hommage poétique à Justine Kamara et au patrimoine culturel guinéen. Plutôt que de prononcer un discours protocolaire classique, le ministre a choisi de griffonner quelques vers pour encourager la candidate et lui rappeler la portée symbolique de sa mission. Évoquant les couleurs nationales, il a présenté le rouge comme le symbole du sang des ancêtres, le jaune comme celui de l’or enfoui dans le sous-sol guinéen et le vert comme l’espérance portée par les forêts du pays. Dans son texte, il a également convoqué les différentes régions de la Guinée, les femmes des marchés, les pêcheurs de Kaloum et les enfants de Kankan, soulignant que la candidate ne serait pas seule sur la scène internationale. « Tu n’es pas seule sur cette scène du monde, Justin Camara. Derrière toi marchent la Basse-Côte et la Haute-Guinée, les femmes des marchés, les pêcheurs de Kaloum, les enfants qui rêvent sous les manguiers de Kankan », a-t-il déclamé. Le ministre a aussi mis en avant la portée culturelle de la Nimba, figure emblématique du patrimoine baga, dont la présence artistique a marqué la cérémonie. Associée à la fécondité, à la fertilité et à la terre nourricière dans son discours, cette figure a été présentée comme l’expression de la richesse des traditions guinéennes. Le ministre Moussa Moïse Sylla a enfin invité Justine Kamara à avancer avec audace et patriotisme, tout en lui rappelant que sa participation constituait déjà une source de fierté nationale. « Reviens-nous plus forte, car, pour nous, tu es déjà une reine : la reine qui a osé porter tout un pays dans un seul sourire », a-t-il lancé, avant de conclure par un vibrant « Allez la Guinée ! Allez Justin ! ». À travers ce cocktail de départ, les organisateurs ont ainsi voulu transformer la participation de Justine Kamara en une aventure collective, portée par la culture, la solidarité et l’ambition de faire rayonner la Guinée au-delà de ses frontières. Le rendez-vous est désormais fixé au 24 novembre 2026, à Porto Rico, où la représentante guinéenne tentera de défendre ses chances face aux candidates du monde entier. items.title: China’s families are now supporting more old people than kids
items.description: Families in China are now supporting more elderly people than children, the government has said. Official data released last week show that the ratio of China’s dependent elderly people to the working-age population rose to 23% last year, overtaking the figure for children, which stood at 22%. The numbers are closely watched for signs of how China’s shrinking workforce will affect both the world’s second-largest economy and global growth. The latest figures mark a significant milestone as China grapples with an ageing population that could affect families, pensions and healthcare spending, analysts say. China has prepared for a growing proportion of elderly people in recent years, while urging younger generations to marry and couples to have more children . The latest data from China’s National Bureau of Statistics show that more than 223 million people in China are aged 65 and above, accounting for nearly 16% of the country’s total population. At the same time, about 213 million children are aged 14 and under. No official commentary accompanied the statistics. But the Chinese state-controlled news outlet Global Times wrote that the nation’s “entry into a moderately ageing society” results from a mix of factors, including the “size of past birth cohorts” and longer life expectancy. The shift could add strain on pension, healthcare, and long-term care systems, while also creating opportunities in the so-called silver economy that caters to older consumers, the newspaper said. “It reflects a historical trend in demographic development rather than a short-term phenomenon,” one researcher told the Global Times. The demographic shift is “symbolic” and could mean more public spending shifts from families and schools to pensions and healthcare, said Professor Stuart Gietel-Basten of The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology. It may also challenge the country’s ambitions, as it could limit economic growth and people’s spending power, said National University of Singapore sociology lecturer Mu Zheng. Birth rates in China have been falling for years now China’s ageing population has been driven by a mix of factors, including rapid urbanisation and the effects of the controversial one-child policy , which was in place from 1980 to the end of 2015. The strategy, designed to keep China’s rapid population growth under control, is estimated by the country’s government to have prevented about 400 million births since it began, though this number has been contested. The policy played a key role in shrinking the population, meaning fewer younger people to support a growing number of elderly relatives, Mu said. But despite easing restrictions on family size, Beijing has struggled to persuade couples to have more children, with birth rates hitting historic lows. Other contributing factors include changing gender roles, rising living costs and higher education levels that have put pressure on fertility rates, Mu said. Beijing also made further support for older people part of its five-year economic blueprint, announced earlier this year. Financial support for pensioners has become an increasingly large part of Chinese government spending. By the end of 2025, more than 53 million elderly people were receiving senior citizen allowances and subsidies, according to official figures. The Global Times noted that many people entering old age who were born between the 1950s and the 1970s generally have higher incomes than previous generations, stronger purchasing power, and are healthier. The dependency ratio is widely used to measure ageing populations, but some experts have questioned it, arguing its scope is too limited. Gietel-Basten said using the statistics risks “taking agency away” from older people, many of whom he says have been misrepresented as dependants. It also fails to account for improvements in healthcare, he added.

items.title: Egypt court fines journalist Lina Attalah and orders news site’s closure
items.description: The editor-in-chief of the independent Egyptian news outlet Mada Masr was detained for several hours after a court convicted her of managing an unlicensed website and ordered its closure, her lawyers say. Mada Masr said Lina Attalah was released after she paid the 3m Egyptian pounds ($53,500; £40,100) fine also handed down by the New Cairo Misdemeanours Court. It was the maximum possible penalty for the charge, which she had rejected. Amnesty International said the verdict represented “a crushing blow to press freedom”. It comes only weeks after six journalists working for the independent fact-checking platform Matsda2sh were charged with belonging to the outlawed Muslim Brotherhood. Egypt is among the top jailers of journalists globally, with 25 currently behind bars, according to the Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ). President Abdul Fattah el-Sisi has overseen what human rights groups say is an unprecedented crackdown on dissent since he led the military’s overthrow of his predecessor, Muslim Brotherhood leader Mohammed Morsi, in 2013. Tens of thousands of people have been detained, mainly Brotherhood officials and supporters, but also leading secular and liberal activists, media workers and academics. The CPJ said Mada Masr, founded in 2013, was a vital source of critical reporting in Egypt and had long faced pressure from authorities over its journalism. The site had repeatedly sought an operating licence from the Supreme Media Regulatory Council (SMRC) since a new media law was passed in 2018, but its applications were either rejected or left unanswered, the media watchdog added. Amnesty International said Lina Attalah had also faced “years of harassment and intimidation”, including six criminal investigations over Mada Masr’s reporting. Last week, prosecutors summoned her for questioning over allegations that she published “false news” and operated a website without a licence. Mada Masr’s lawyer said the investigation included a recent report the website published about a wave of protests in prisons across the country, as well as a letter from the SMRC on its legal status. Attalah was released on bail and later referred to trial before the New Cairo Misdemeanours Court on the charge of operating a website without a licence. During Tuesday’s hearing, Judge Mohammed Mubarak ordered the courtroom to be cleared of everyone except Attalah, her eight-person defence team, and Hossam Bahgat, head of the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights (EIPR), an independent human rights group. Bahgat told AFP that security personnel then filed in before the judge announced the court was denying several procedural requests made by the defence and appointing its own lawyer for Attalah. “In a move that astonished all those present, the judge recorded in the official court minutes that the court had appointed a lawyer from the Lawyers’ Syndicate to represent the defence,” he said. “Lina herself spoke up to object to this lawyer being appointed to represent her, which the judge refused to record in the court minutes. “In an even more shocking turn, the judge proceeded to dictate motions on behalf of this lawyer – who had not uttered a single word – and entered them into the official record,” he added. The judge then announced the fine for Attalah and ordered Mada Masr’s closure “amid shouts and protests from the defence”, before she was detained, according to Bahgat. On Tuesday evening, Mada Masr said it had paid the full fine to the court and that Attalah was released after several hours in custody. “During the release procedures, Attalah learned of a one-year prison sentence issued against her in absentia in 2024, on charges of publishing false news and managing an unlicensed website,” it added. “Her lawyers took steps to challenge the ruling, with a hearing in a retrial of the case scheduled for 11 November.” Amnesty International warned that the court’s verdict marked “a dark day for independent journalism” in Egypt and demanded that it be overturned. “This draconian ruling is the culmination of years of relentless harassment and unjust proceedings designed to shut down one of the country’s last remaining independent media voices,” said the group’s senior director for regional impact, Yasmine Ahmed. “Lina Attalah should never have been prosecuted for exercising her right to freedom of expression and doing her journalistic job.” CPJ Regional Director Sara Qudah said: “If Egypt can put in custody one of its most respected editors and shut down her newsroom, no independent journalist in the country is safe. Attalah must be released immediately, and Mada Masr must be allowed to keep reporting.”

items.title: Sénégal – Drame à Ziguinchor : Un commerçant retrouvé mort pendu après la perte de 800 000 F CFA
items.description: Image d'illustration Un drame s'est produit à Ziguinchor ce lundi 26 octobre 2026, où A. Diallo, un commerçant d'environ 27 ans domicilié au quartier Néma 2, a été retrouvé mort pendu dans une boutique située sur le Boulevard 54 mètres. Alerté dans la mi-journée, le commissariat central de Ziguinchor a ouvert une enquête sous l'autorité du Procureur près le Tribunal de Grande Instance pour éclaircir les circonstances du décès, survenu après que le jeune homme s'est confié à son entourage sur la perte récente d'une somme de 800 000 F CFA. La tranquillité du Boulevard 54 mètres à Ziguinchor a été brutalement interrompue dans la matinée du lundi 26 octobre 2026. Aux alentours de 11 heures, L. Diallo, le propriétaire d'une boutique locale, s'est rendu sur les lieux pour rendre visite au commerçant. C'est alors qu'il a fait la découverte du corps d'A. Diallo, suspendu au plafond à l'aide d'un fil de couleur noire. Informé par appel téléphonique à 13 heures 30 minutes, le commissariat central de Ziguinchor a immédiatement dépêché des éléments sur place. La victime, âgée d'environ 27 ans et domiciliée au quartier Néma 2, a été formellement identifiée par les forces de l'ordre. Auditionnés par les enquêteurs, les proches du défunt ont apporté de premiers éléments de contexte sur sa situation personnelle. Le propriétaire des lieux, L. Diallo, a confirmé avoir découvert la scène aux environs de 11 heures. De son côté, M. Diallo, cousin du défunt, a expliqué aux policiers que le jeune homme faisait face à d'importants soucis d'argent. Selon des informations rapportées par Seneweb , A. Diallo lui avait confié avoir perdu la somme de huit cent mille (800 000) F CFA. Le cousin a toutefois souligné que la victime n'avait jamais exprimé d'intentions suicidaires par le passé. Afin d'éclaircir les circonstances exactes de ce drame, des actes médico-légaux et judiciaires ont été ordonnés. La dépouille sans vie a été acheminée vers l'Hôpital régional de Ziguinchor, où une autopsie doit être pratiquée. Informé des faits, le Procureur près le Tribunal de Grande Instance (TGI) de Ziguinchor a ordonné l'ouverture d'une enquête confiée aux services de police. L’article Sénégal – Drame à Ziguinchor : Un commerçant retrouvé mort pendu après la perte de 800 000 F CFA est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .
